### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FComicStory" title="http://schema.org/ComicStory"></a> Class: ComicStory <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ComicStory)</small>

The term "story" is any indivisible, re-printable unit of a comic, including the interior stories, covers, and backmatter. Most comics have at least two stories: a cover (ComicCoverArt) and an interior story.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FComment" title="http://schema.org/Comment"></a> Class: Comment <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Comment)</small>

A comment on an item - for example, a comment on a blog post. The comment's content is expressed via the [[text]] property, and its topic via [[about]], properties shared with all CreativeWorks.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCompleteDataFeed" title="http://schema.org/CompleteDataFeed"></a> Class: CompleteDataFeed <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/CompleteDataFeed)</small>

A [[CompleteDataFeed]] is a [[DataFeed]] whose standard representation includes content for every item currently in the feed. This is the equivalent of Atom's element as defined in Feed Paging and Archiving [RFC 5005](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5005), for example (and as defined for Atom), when using data from a feed that represents a collection of items that varies over time (e.g. "Top Twenty Records") there is no need to have newer entries mixed in alongside older, obsolete entries. By marking this feed as a CompleteDataFeed, old entries can be safely discarded when the feed is refreshed, since we can assume the feed has provided descriptions for all current items.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCompoundPriceSpecification" title="http://schema.org/CompoundPriceSpecification"></a> Class: CompoundPriceSpecification <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/CompoundPriceSpecification)</small>

A compound price specification is one that bundles multiple prices that all apply in combination for different dimensions of consumption. Use the name property of the attached unit price specification for indicating the dimension of a price component (e.g. "electricity" or "final cleaning").

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

#### Properties from Thing

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FConstraintNode" title="http://schema.org/ConstraintNode"></a> Class: ConstraintNode <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ConstraintNode)</small>

The ConstraintNode type is provided to support usecases in which a node in a structured data graph is described with properties which appear to describe a single entity, but are being used in a situation where they serve a more abstract purpose. A [[ConstraintNode]] can be described using [[constraintProperty]] and [[numConstraints]]. These constraint properties can serve a variety of purposes, and their values may sometimes be understood to indicate sets of possible values rather than single, exact and specific values.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

For example, in the definition of a [[StatisticalVariable]]. The value is a property, either from within Schema.org or from other compatible (e.g. RDF) systems such as DataCommons.org or Wikidata.org.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProperty" title="http://schema.org/Property">Property</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FnumConstraints" title="http://schema.org/numConstraints">numConstraints</a> | No | Indicates the number of constraints property values defined for a particular [[ConstraintNode]] such as [[StatisticalVariable]]. This helps applications understand if they have access to a sufficiently complete description of a [[StatisticalVariable]] or other construct that is defined using properties on template-style nodes. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FInteger" title="http://schema.org/Integer">Integer</a> |  |

Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FConversation" title="http://schema.org/Conversation"></a> Class: Conversation <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Conversation)</small>

One or more messages between organizations or people on a particular topic. Individual messages can be linked to the conversation with isPartOf or hasPart properties.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| N/A | N/A |

The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCourse" title="http://schema.org/Course"></a> Class: Course <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Course)</small>

A description of an educational course which may be offered as distinct instances which take place at different times or take place at different locations, or be offered through different media or modes of study. An educational course is a sequence of one or more educational events and/or creative works which aims to build knowledge, competence or ability of learners.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCourseInstance" title="http://schema.org/CourseInstance"></a> Class: CourseInstance <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/CourseInstance)</small>

An instance of a [[Course]] which is distinct from other instances because it is offered at a different time or location or through different media or modes of study or to a specific section of students.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCovidTestingFacility" title="http://schema.org/CovidTestingFacility"></a> Class: CovidTestingFacility <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/CovidTestingFacility)</small>

A CovidTestingFacility is a [[MedicalClinic]] where testing for the COVID-19 Coronavirus disease is available. If the facility is being made available from an established [[Pharmacy]], [[Hotel]], or other non-medical organization, multiple types can be listed. This makes it easier to re-use existing schema.org information about that place, e.g. contact info, address, opening hours. Note that in an emergency, such information may not always be reliable. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCreativeWork" title="http://schema.org/CreativeWork"></a> Class: CreativeWork <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/CreativeWork)</small>

The most generic kind of creative work, including books, movies, photographs, software programs, etc.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCreativeWorkSeries" title="http://schema.org/CreativeWorkSeries"></a> Class: CreativeWorkSeries <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/CreativeWorkSeries)</small>

A CreativeWorkSeries in schema.org is a group of related items, typically but not necessarily of the same kind. CreativeWorkSeries are usually organized into some order, often chronological. Unlike [[ItemList]] which is a general purpose data structure for lists of things, the emphasis with CreativeWorkSeries is on published materials (written e.g. books and periodicals, or media such as TV, radio and games).\n\nSpecific subtypes are available for describing [[TVSeries]], [[RadioSeries]], [[MovieSeries]], [[BookSeries]], [[Periodical]] and [[VideoGameSeries]]. In each case, the [[hasPart]] / [[isPartOf]] properties can be used to relate the CreativeWorkSeries to its parts. The general CreativeWorkSeries type serves largely just to organize these more specific and practical subtypes.\n\nIt is common for properties applicable to an item from the series to be usefully applied to the containing group. Schema.org attempts to anticipate some of these cases, but publishers should be free to apply properties of the series parts to the series as a whole wherever they seem appropriate. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCredential" title="http://schema.org/Credential"></a> Class: Credential <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Credential)</small>

A credential is a certificate that is used to verify the identity of a person or entity.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCreditCard" title="http://schema.org/CreditCard"></a> Class: CreditCard <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/CreditCard)</small>

A card payment method of a particular brand or name. Used to mark up a particular payment method and/or the financial product/service that supplies the card account.\n\nCommonly used values:\n\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#AmericanExpress\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DinersClub\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Discover\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#JCB\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#MasterCard\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#VISA 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |

| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCriticReview" title="http://schema.org/CriticReview"></a> Class: CriticReview <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/CriticReview)</small>

A [[CriticReview]] is a more specialized form of Review written or published by a source that is recognized for its reviewing activities. These can include online columns, travel and food guides, TV and radio shows, blogs and other independent Web sites. [[CriticReview]]s are typically more in-depth and professionally written. For simpler, casually written user/visitor/viewer/customer reviews, it is more appropriate to use the [[UserReview]] type. Review aggregator sites such as Metacritic already separate out the site's user reviews from selected critic reviews that originate from third-party sources.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDDxElement" title="http://schema.org/DDxElement"></a> Class: DDxElement <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/DDxElement)</small>

An alternative, closely-related condition typically considered later in the differential diagnosis process along with the signs that are used to distinguish it.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmeasurementTechnique" title="http://schema.org/measurementTechnique">measurementTechnique</a> | No | A technique, method or technology used in an [[Observation]], [[StatisticalVariable]] or [[Dataset]] (or [[DataDownload]], [[DataCatalog]]), corresponding to the method used for measuring the corresponding variable(s) (for datasets, described using [[variableMeasured]]; for [[Observation]], a [[StatisticalVariable]]). Often but not necessarily each [[variableMeasured]] will have an explicit representation as (or mapping to) an property such as those defined in Schema.org, or other RDF vocabularies and "knowledge graphs". In that case the subproperty of [[variableMeasured]] called [[measuredProperty]] is applicable. The [[measurementTechnique]] property helps when extra clarification is needed about how a [[measuredProperty]] was measured. This is oriented towards scientific and scholarly dataset publication but may have broader applicability; it is not intended as a full representation of measurement, but can often serve as a high level summary for dataset discovery. For example, if [[variableMeasured]] is: molecule concentration, [[measurementTechnique]] could be: "mass spectrometry" or "nmr spectroscopy" or "colorimetry" or "immunofluorescence". If the [[variableMeasured]] is "depression rating", the [[measurementTechnique]] could be "Zung Scale" or "HAM-D" or "Beck Depression Inventory". If there are several [[variableMeasured]] properties recorded for some given data object, use a [[PropertyValue]] for each [[variableMeasured]] and attach the corresponding [[measurementTechnique]]. The value can also be from an enumeration, organized as a [[MeasurementMethodEnum]]. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDefinedTerm" title="http://schema.org/DefinedTerm">DefinedTerm</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMeasurementMethodEnum" title="http://schema.org/MeasurementMethodEnum">MeasurementMethodEnum</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmeasurementTechnique" title="http://schema.org/measurementTechnique">measurementTechnique</a> | No | A technique, method or technology used in an [[Observation]], [[StatisticalVariable]] or [[Dataset]] (or [[DataDownload]], [[DataCatalog]]), corresponding to the method used for measuring the corresponding variable(s) (for datasets, described using [[variableMeasured]]; for [[Observation]], a [[StatisticalVariable]]). Often but not necessarily each [[variableMeasured]] will have an explicit representation as (or mapping to) an property such as those defined in Schema.org, or other RDF vocabularies and "knowledge graphs". In that case the subproperty of [[variableMeasured]] called [[measuredProperty]] is applicable. The [[measurementTechnique]] property helps when extra clarification is needed about how a [[measuredProperty]] was measured. This is oriented towards scientific and scholarly dataset publication but may have broader applicability; it is not intended as a full representation of measurement, but can often serve as a high level summary for dataset discovery. For example, if [[variableMeasured]] is: molecule concentration, [[measurementTechnique]] could be: "mass spectrometry" or "nmr spectroscopy" or "colorimetry" or "immunofluorescence". If the [[variableMeasured]] is "depression rating", the [[measurementTechnique]] could be "Zung Scale" or "HAM-D" or "Beck Depression Inventory". If there are several [[variableMeasured]] properties recorded for some given data object, use a [[PropertyValue]] for each [[variableMeasured]] and attach the corresponding [[measurementTechnique]]. A maintainer is a [[Person]] or [[Organization]] that manages contributions to, and/or publication of, some (typically complex) artifact. It is common for distributions of software and data to be based on "upstream" sources. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmaterialExtent" title="http://schema.org/materialExtent">materialExtent</a> | No | The quantity of the materials being described or an expression of the physical space they occupy. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmentions" title="http://schema.org/mentions">mentions</a> | No | Indicates that the CreativeWork contains a reference to, but is not necessarily about a concept. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FThing" title="http://schema.org/Thing">Thing</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Foffers" title="http://schema.org/offers">offers</a> | No | An offer to provide this item&#x2014;for example, an offer to sell a product, rent the DVD of a movie, perform a service, or give away tickets to an event. Use [[businessFunction]] to indicate the kind of transaction offered, i.e. sell, lease, etc. This property can also be used to describe a [[Demand]]. While this property is listed as expected on a number of common types, it can be used in others. In that case, using a second type, such as Product or a subtype of Product, can clarify the nature of the offer.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDemand" title="http://schema.org/Demand">Demand</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOffer" title="http://schema.org/Offer">Offer</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FtemporalCoverage" title="http://schema.org/temporalCoverage">temporalCoverage</a> | No | The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in [ISO 8601 time interval format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals). In the case of a Dataset it will typically indicate the relevant time period in a precise notation (e.g. for a 2011 census dataset, the year 2011 would be written "2011/2012"). Other forms of content, e.g. ScholarlyArticle, Book, TVSeries or TVEpisode, may indicate their temporalCoverage in broader terms - textually or via well-known URL. Open-ended date ranges can be written with ".." in place of the end date. For example, "2015-11/.." indicates a range beginning in November 2015 and with no specified final date. This is tentative and might be updated in future when ISO 8601 is officially updated. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDateTime" title="http://schema.org/DateTime">DateTime</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

This property can be used alongside the license property which indicates license(s) applicable to some piece of content. The day of the week, e.g. used to specify to which day the opening hours of an OpeningHoursSpecification refer. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDefinedRegion" title="http://schema.org/DefinedRegion"></a> Class: DefinedRegion <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/DefinedRegion)</small>

A DefinedRegion is a geographic area defined by potentially arbitrary (rather than political, administrative or natural geographical) criteria. Properties are provided for defining a region by reference to sets of postal codes. Examples: a delivery destination when shopping. Region where regional pricing is configured. Requirement 1: Country: US States: "NY", "CA" Requirement 2: Country: US PostalCode Set: { [94000-94585], [97000, 97999], [13000, 13599]} { [12345, 12345], [78945, 78945], } Region = state, canton, prefecture, autonomous community... 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDefinedTerm" title="http://schema.org/DefinedTerm"></a> Class: DefinedTerm <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/DefinedTerm)</small>

A word, name, acronym, phrase, etc. with a formal definition. Often used in the context of category or subject classification, glossaries or dictionaries, product or creative work types, etc. Use the name property for the term being defined, use termCode if the term has an alpha-numeric code allocated, use description to provide the definition of the term. Use the about property to specify what the term is about.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDeliveryChargeSpecification" title="http://schema.org/DeliveryChargeSpecification"></a> Class: DeliveryChargeSpecification <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/DeliveryChargeSpecification)</small>

The price for the delivery of an offer using a particular delivery method.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDeliveryMethod" title="http://schema.org/DeliveryMethod"></a> Class: DeliveryMethod <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/DeliveryMethod)</small>

A delivery method is a standardized procedure for transferring the product or service to the destination of fulfillment chosen by the customer. Delivery methods are characterized by the means of transportation used, and by the organization or group that is the contracting party for the sending organization or person.\n\nCommonly used values:\n\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeDirectDownload\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeFreight\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeMail\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeOwnFleet\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModePickUp\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DHL\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#FederalExpress\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#UPS 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDemand" title="http://schema.org/Demand"></a> Class: Demand <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Demand)</small>

A demand entity represents the public, not necessarily binding, not necessarily exclusive, announcement by an organization or person to seek a certain type of goods or services. For describing demand using this type, the very same properties used for Offer apply.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDiagnosticProcedure" title="http://schema.org/DiagnosticProcedure"></a> Class: DiagnosticProcedure <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/DiagnosticProcedure)</small>

A medical procedure intended primarily for diagnostic, as opposed to therapeutic, purposes.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDiet" title="http://schema.org/Diet"></a> Class: Diet <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Diet)</small>

A strategy of regulating the intake of food to achieve or maintain a specific health-related goal.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDietarySupplement" title="http://schema.org/DietarySupplement"></a> Class: DietarySupplement <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/DietarySupplement)</small>

A product taken by mouth that contains a dietary ingredient intended to supplement the diet. Dietary ingredients may include vitamins, minerals, herbs or other botanicals, amino acids, and substances such as enzymes, organ tissues, glandulars and metabolites.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Note also that this is a definition for how to include GTINs in Schema.org data, and not a definition of GTINs in general - see the GS1 documentation for authoritative details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmobileUrl" title="http://schema.org/mobileUrl">mobileUrl</a> | No | The [[mobileUrl]] property is provided for specific situations in which data consumers need to determine whether one of several provided URLs is a dedicated 'mobile site'. The general trend in web technology is towards [responsive design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsive_web_design) in which content can be flexibly adapted to a wide range of browsing environments. Pages and sites referenced with the long-established [[url]] property should ideally also be usable on a wide variety of devices, including mobile phones. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDigitalPlatformEnumeration" title="http://schema.org/DigitalPlatformEnumeration"></a> Class: DigitalPlatformEnumeration <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/DigitalPlatformEnumeration)</small>

Enumerates some common technology platforms, for use with properties such as [[actionPlatform]]. It is not supposed to be comprehensive - when a suitable code is not enumerated here, textual or URL values can be used instead. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDrug" title="http://schema.org/Drug"></a> Class: Drug <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Drug)</small>

A chemical or biologic substance, used as a medical therapy, that has a physiological effect on an organism. Here the term drug is used interchangeably with the term medicine although clinical knowledge makes a clear difference between them.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmobileUrl" title="http://schema.org/mobileUrl">mobileUrl</a> | No | The [[mobileUrl]] property is provided for specific situations in which data consumers need to determine whether one of several provided URLs is a dedicated 'mobile site'. The general trend in web technology is towards [responsive design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsive_web_design) in which content can be flexibly adapted to a wide range of browsing environments. Pages and sites referenced with the long-established [[url]] property should ideally also be usable on a wide variety of devices, including mobile phones. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDrugCost" title="http://schema.org/DrugCost"></a> Class: DrugCost <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/DrugCost)</small>

The cost per unit of a medical drug. Note that this type is not meant to represent the price in an offer of a drug for sale; see the Offer type for that. This type will typically be used to tag wholesale or average retail cost of a drug, or maximum reimbursable cost. Costs of medical drugs vary widely depending on how and where they are paid for, so while this type captures some of the variables, costs should be used with caution by consumers of this schema's markup.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmaintainer" title="http://schema.org/maintainer">maintainer</a> | No | A maintainer of a [[Dataset]], software package ([[SoftwareApplication]]), or other [[Project]]. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FEducationalOccupationalProgram" title="http://schema.org/EducationalOccupationalProgram"></a> Class: EducationalOccupationalProgram <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/EducationalOccupationalProgram)</small>

A program offered by an institution which determines the learning progress to achieve an outcome, usually a credential like a degree or certificate. This would define a discrete set of opportunities (e.g., job, courses) that together constitute a program with a clear start, end, set of requirements, and transition to a new occupational opportunity (e.g., a job), or sometimes a higher educational opportunity (e.g., an advanced degree).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The identifier should be in the `XXXX:YYYYYY:ZZZ` or `XXXX:YYYYYY`format. Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FEmployerReview" title="http://schema.org/EmployerReview"></a> Class: EmployerReview <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/EmployerReview)</small>

An [[EmployerReview]] is a review of an [[Organization]] regarding its role as an employer, written by a current or former employee of that organization.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FEndorsementRating" title="http://schema.org/EndorsementRating"></a> Class: EndorsementRating <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/EndorsementRating)</small>

An EndorsementRating is a rating that expresses some level of endorsement, for example inclusion in a "critic's pick" blog, a "Like" or "+1" on a social network. It can be considered the [[result]] of an [[EndorseAction]] in which the [[object]] of the action is rated positively by some [[agent]]. As is common elsewhere in schema.org, it is sometimes more useful to describe the results of such an action without explicitly describing the [[Action]]. An [[EndorsementRating]] may be part of a numeric scale or organized system, but this is not required: having an explicit type for indicating a positive, endorsement rating is particularly useful in the absence of numeric scales as it helps consumers understand that the rating is broadly positive. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

Please note that author is special in that HTML 5 provides a special mechanism for indicating authorship via the rel tag. That is equivalent to this and may be used interchangeably. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FEnergyConsumptionDetails" title="http://schema.org/EnergyConsumptionDetails"></a> Class: EnergyConsumptionDetails <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/EnergyConsumptionDetails)</small>

EnergyConsumptionDetails represents information related to the energy efficiency of a product that consumes energy. The information that can be provided is based on international regulations such as for example [EU directive 2017/1369](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2017/1369/oj) for energy labeling and the [Energy labeling rule](https://www.ftc.gov/enforcement/rules/rulemaking-regulatory-reform-proceedings/energy-water-use-labeling-consumer) under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (EPCA) in the US.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FenergyEfficiencyScaleMax" title="http://schema.org/energyEfficiencyScaleMax">energyEfficiencyScaleMax</a> | No | Specifies the most energy efficient class on the regulated EU energy consumption scale for the product category a product belongs to. For example, energy consumption for televisions placed on the market after January 1, 2020 is scaled from D to A+++. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FEUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration" title="http://schema.org/EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration">EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration</a> |  |

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FEventReservation" title="http://schema.org/EventReservation"></a> Class: EventReservation <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/EventReservation)</small>

A reservation for an event like a concert, sporting event, or lecture.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FEventSeries" title="http://schema.org/EventSeries"></a> Class: EventSeries <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/EventSeries)</small>

A series of [[Event]]s. Included events can relate with the series using the [[superEvent]] property. An EventSeries is a collection of events that share some unifying characteristic. For example, "The Olympic Games" is a series, which is repeated regularly. The "2012 London Olympics" can be presented both as an [[Event]] in the series "Olympic Games", and as an [[EventSeries]] that included a number of sporting competitions as Events. The nature of the association between the events in an [[EventSeries]] can vary, but typical examples could include a thematic event series (e.g. topical meetups or classes), or a series of regular events that share a location, attendee group and/or organizers. EventSeries has been defined as a kind of Event to make it easy for publishers to use it in an Event context without worrying about which kinds of series are really event-like enough to call an Event. In general an EventSeries may seem more Event-like when the period of time is compact and when aspects such as location are fixed, but it may also sometimes prove useful to describe a longer-term series as an Event. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |

Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FExercisePlan" title="http://schema.org/ExercisePlan"></a> Class: ExercisePlan <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ExercisePlan)</small>

Fitness-related activity designed for a specific health-related purpose, including defined exercise routines as well as activity prescribed by a clinician.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FFAQPage" title="http://schema.org/FAQPage"></a> Class: FAQPage <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/FAQPage)</small>

A [[FAQPage]] is a [[WebPage]] presenting one or more "[Frequently asked questions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FAQ)" (see also [[QAPage]]).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasCredential" title="http://schema.org/hasCredential">hasCredential</a> | No | A credential awarded to the Person or Organization. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCredential" title="http://schema.org/Credential">Credential</a> |  |

This URL should conform to the particular requirements of digital links. The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FFinancialIncentive" title="http://schema.org/FinancialIncentive"></a> Class: FinancialIncentive <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/FinancialIncentive)</small>

<p>Represents financial incentives for goods/services offered by an organization (or individual).</p> <p>Typically contains the [[name]] of the incentive, the [[incentivizedItem]], the [[incentiveAmount]], the [[incentiveStatus]], [[incentiveType]], the [[provider]] of the incentive, and [[eligibleWithSupplier]].</p> <p>Optionally contains criteria on whether the incentive is limited based on [[purchaseType]], [[purchasePriceLimit]], [[incomeLimit]], and the [[qualifiedExpense]]. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

#### Properties from FinancialIncentive

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FareaServed" title="http://schema.org/areaServed">areaServed</a> | No | The geographic area where a service or offered item is provided. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FAdministrativeArea" title="http://schema.org/AdministrativeArea">AdministrativeArea</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FGeoShape" title="http://schema.org/GeoShape">GeoShape</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPlace" title="http://schema.org/Place">Place</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FeligibleWithSupplier" title="http://schema.org/eligibleWithSupplier">eligibleWithSupplier</a> | No | The supplier of the incentivized item/service for which the incentive is valid for such as a utility company, merchant, or contractor. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FincentiveAmount" title="http://schema.org/incentiveAmount">incentiveAmount</a> | No | Describes the amount that can be redeemed from this incentive. <p>[[QuantitativeValue]]: Use this for incentives based on price (either raw amount or percentage-based). For a raw amount example, "You can claim $2,500 - $7,500 from the total cost of installation" would be represented as the following:</p> { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", “minValue”: 2500, “maxValue”: 7500, "unitCode": "USD" } <p>[[QuantitativeValue]] can also be used for percentage amounts. In such cases, value is used to represent the incentive’s percentage, while maxValue represents a limit (if one exists) to that incentive. The unitCode should be 'P1' and the unitText should be '%', while valueReference should be used for holding the currency type. For example, "You can claim up to 30% of the total cost of installation, up to a maximum of $7,500" would be:</p> { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", "value": 30, "unitCode": "P1", "unitText": "%", “maxValue”: 7500, “valueReference”: “USD” } <p>[[UnitPriceSpecification]]: Use this for incentives that are based on amounts rather than price. For example, a net metering rebate that pays $10/kWh, up to $1,000:</p> { "@type": "UnitPriceSpecification", "price": 10, "priceCurrency": "USD", "referenceQuantity": 1, "unitCode": "DO3", "unitText": "kw/h", "maxPrice": 1000, "description": "$10 / kwh up to $1000" } <p>[[LoanOrCredit]]: Use for incentives that are loan based. For example, a loan of $4,000 - $50,000 with a repayment term of 10 years, interest free would look like:</p> { "@type": "LoanOrCredit", "loanTerm": { "@type":"QuantitativeValue", "value":"10", "unitCode": "ANN" }, "amount":[ { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", "Name":"fixed interest rate", "value":"0", }, ], "amount":[ { "@type": "MonetaryAmount", "Name":"min loan amount", "value":"4000", "currency":"CAD" }, { "@type": "MonetaryAmount", "Name":"max loan amount", "value":"50000", "currency":"CAD" } ], } In summary: <ul><li>Use [[QuantitativeValue]] for absolute/percentage-based incentives applied on the price of a good/service.</li> <li>Use [[UnitPriceSpecification]] for incentives based on a per-unit basis (e.g. net metering).</li> <li>Use [[LoanOrCredit]] for loans/credits.</li> </ul>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLoanOrCredit" title="http://schema.org/LoanOrCredit">LoanOrCredit</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FUnitPriceSpecification" title="http://schema.org/UnitPriceSpecification">UnitPriceSpecification</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FincentiveStatus" title="http://schema.org/incentiveStatus">incentiveStatus</a> | No | The status of the incentive (active, on hold, retired, etc.). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FIncentiveStatus" title="http://schema.org/IncentiveStatus">IncentiveStatus</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FincentiveType" title="http://schema.org/incentiveType">incentiveType</a> | No | The type of incentive offered (tax credit/rebate, tax deduction, tax waiver, subsidies, etc.). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FIncentiveType" title="http://schema.org/IncentiveType">IncentiveType</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FincentivizedItem" title="http://schema.org/incentivizedItem">incentivizedItem</a> | No | The type or specific product(s) and/or service(s) being incentivized. <p>DefinedTermSets are used for product and service categories such as the United Nations Standard Products and Services Code:</p> { "@type": "DefinedTerm", "inDefinedTermSet": "https://www.unspsc.org/", "termCode": "261315XX", "name": "Photovoltaic module" } <p>For a specific product or service, use the Product type:</p> { "@type": "Product", "name": "Kenmore White 17" Microwave", } For multiple different incentivized items, use multiple [[DefinedTerm]] or [[Product]]. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDefinedTerm" title="http://schema.org/DefinedTerm">DefinedTerm</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProduct" title="http://schema.org/Product">Product</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fprovider" title="http://schema.org/provider">provider</a> | No | The service provider, service operator, or service performer; the goods producer. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FFloorPlan" title="http://schema.org/FloorPlan"></a> Class: FloorPlan <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/FloorPlan)</small>

A FloorPlan is an explicit representation of a collection of similar accommodations, allowing the provision of common information (room counts, sizes, layout diagrams) and offers for rental or sale. In typical use, some [[ApartmentComplex]] has an [[accommodationFloorPlan]] which is a [[FloorPlan]]. A FloorPlan is always in the context of a particular place, either a larger [[ApartmentComplex]] or a single [[Apartment]]. The visual/spatial aspects of a floor plan (i.e. room layout, [see wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floor_plan)) can be indicated using [[image]]. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FFollowAction" title="http://schema.org/FollowAction"></a> Class: FollowAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/FollowAction)</small>

The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates polled from.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[BefriendAction]]: Unlike BefriendAction, FollowAction implies that the connection is *not* necessarily reciprocal.\n* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, FollowAction implies that the follower acts as an active agent constantly/actively polling for updates.\n* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.\n* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in getting updates from the object.\n* [[TrackAction]]: Unlike TrackAction, FollowAction refers to the polling of updates of all aspects of animate objects rather than the location of inanimate objects (e.g. you track a package, but you don't follow it).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FFoodEstablishmentReservation" title="http://schema.org/FoodEstablishmentReservation"></a> Class: FoodEstablishmentReservation <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/FoodEstablishmentReservation)</small>

A reservation to dine at a food-related business.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FFundingAgency" title="http://schema.org/FundingAgency"></a> Class: FundingAgency <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/FundingAgency)</small>

A FundingAgency is an organization that implements one or more [[FundingScheme]]s and manages the granting process (via [[Grant]]s, typically [[MonetaryGrant]]s). A funding agency is not always required for grant funding, e.g. philanthropic giving, corporate sponsorship etc. Examples of funding agencies include ERC, REA, NIH, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, ... 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FFundingScheme" title="http://schema.org/FundingScheme"></a> Class: FundingScheme <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/FundingScheme)</small>

A FundingScheme combines organizational, project and policy aspects of grant-based funding that sets guidelines, principles and mechanisms to support other kinds of projects and activities. Funding is typically organized via [[Grant]] funding. Examples of funding schemes: Swiss Priority Programmes (SPPs); EU Framework 7 (FP7); Horizon 2020; the NIH-R01 Grant Program; Wellcome institutional strategic support fund. For large scale public sector funding, the management and administration of grant awards is often handled by other, dedicated, organizations - [[FundingAgency]]s such as ERC, REA, ...

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FGame" title="http://schema.org/Game"></a> Class: Game <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Game)</small>

The Game type represents things which are games. These are typically rule-governed recreational activities, e.g. role-playing games in which players assume the role of characters in a fictional setting.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FGene" title="http://schema.org/Gene"></a> Class: Gene <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Gene)</small>

A discrete unit of inheritance which affects one or more biological traits (Source: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)). Examples include FOXP2 (Forkhead box protein P2), SCARNA21 (small Cajal body-specific RNA 21), A- (agouti genotype).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FGeoCircle" title="http://schema.org/GeoCircle"></a> Class: GeoCircle <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/GeoCircle)</small>

A GeoCircle is a GeoShape representing a circular geographic area. As it is a GeoShape it provides the simple textual property 'circle', but also allows the combination of postalCode alongside geoRadius. The center of the circle can be indicated via the 'geoMidpoint' property, or more approximately using 'address', 'postalCode'. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FGeoShape" title="http://schema.org/GeoShape"></a> Class: GeoShape <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/GeoShape)</small>

The geographic shape of a place. A GeoShape can be described using several properties whose values are based on latitude/longitude pairs. Either whitespace or commas can be used to separate latitude and longitude; whitespace should be used when writing a list of several such points.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| N/A | N/A |

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| --------- | --------- |

As defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FGeospatialGeometry" title="http://schema.org/GeospatialGeometry">GeospatialGeometry</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPlace" title="http://schema.org/Place">Place</a> |  |

As defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FGeospatialGeometry" title="http://schema.org/GeospatialGeometry">GeospatialGeometry</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPlace" title="http://schema.org/Place">Place</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FgeoCovers" title="http://schema.org/geoCovers">geoCovers</a> | No | Represents a relationship between two geometries (or the places they represent), relating a covering geometry to a covered geometry. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FGiveAction" title="http://schema.org/GiveAction"></a> Class: GiveAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/GiveAction)</small>

The act of transferring ownership of an object to a destination. Reciprocal of TakeAction.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[TakeAction]]: Reciprocal of GiveAction.\n* [[SendAction]]: Unlike SendAction, GiveAction implies that ownership is being transferred (e.g. I may send my laptop to you, but that doesn't mean I'm giving it to you).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FfloorLevel" title="http://schema.org/floorLevel">floorLevel</a> | No | The floor level for an [[Accommodation]] in a multi-storey building. Since counting systems [vary internationally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storey#Consecutive_number_floor_designations), the local system should be used where possible. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FopeningHours" title="http://schema.org/openingHours">openingHours</a> | No | The general opening hours for a business. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FopeningHours" title="http://schema.org/openingHours">openingHours</a> | No | The general opening hours for a business. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FGrant" title="http://schema.org/Grant"></a> Class: Grant <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Grant)</small>

A grant, typically financial or otherwise quantifiable, of resources. Typically a [[funder]] sponsors some [[MonetaryAmount]] to an [[Organization]] or [[Person]], sometimes not necessarily via a dedicated or long-lived [[Project]], resulting in one or more outputs, or [[fundedItem]]s. For financial sponsorship, indicate the [[funder]] of a [[MonetaryGrant]]. For non-financial support, indicate [[sponsor]] of [[Grant]]s of resources (e.g. office space). Grants support activities directed towards some agreed collective goals, often but not always organized as [[Project]]s. Long-lived projects are sometimes sponsored by a variety of grants over time, but it is also common for a project to be associated with a single grant. The amount of a [[Grant]] is represented using [[amount]] as a [[MonetaryAmount]]. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FGuide" title="http://schema.org/Guide"></a> Class: Guide <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Guide)</small>

[[Guide]] is a page or article that recommends specific products or services, or aspects of a thing for a user to consider. A [[Guide]] may represent a Buying Guide and detail aspects of products or services for a user to consider. A [[Guide]] may represent a Product Guide and recommend specific products or services. A [[Guide]] may represent a Ranked List and recommend specific products or services with ranking.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasMemberProgram" title="http://schema.org/hasMemberProgram">hasMemberProgram</a> | No | MemberProgram offered by an Organization, for example an eCommerce merchant or an airline. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMemberProgram" title="http://schema.org/MemberProgram">MemberProgram</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasMerchantReturnPolicy" title="http://schema.org/hasMerchantReturnPolicy">hasMerchantReturnPolicy</a> | No | Specifies a MerchantReturnPolicy that may be applicable. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMerchantReturnPolicy" title="http://schema.org/MerchantReturnPolicy">MerchantReturnPolicy</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasOfferCatalog" title="http://schema.org/hasOfferCatalog">hasOfferCatalog</a> | No | Indicates an OfferCatalog listing for this Organization, Person, or Service. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOfferCatalog" title="http://schema.org/OfferCatalog">OfferCatalog</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasPOS" title="http://schema.org/hasPOS">hasPOS</a> | No | Points-of-Sales operated by the organization or person. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPlace" title="http://schema.org/Place">Place</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasShippingService" title="http://schema.org/hasShippingService">hasShippingService</a> | No | Specification of a shipping service offered by the organization. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FShippingService" title="http://schema.org/ShippingService">ShippingService</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The identifier should be in the `XXXX:YYYYYY:ZZZ` or `XXXX:YYYYYY`format. Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
