| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The identifier should be in the `XXXX:YYYYYY:ZZZ` or `XXXX:YYYYYY`format. Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FHealthAspectEnumeration" title="http://schema.org/HealthAspectEnumeration"></a> Class: HealthAspectEnumeration <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/HealthAspectEnumeration)</small>

HealthAspectEnumeration enumerates several aspects of health content online, each of which might be described using [[hasHealthAspect]] and [[HealthTopicContent]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| N/A | N/A |

Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FHealthTopicContent" title="http://schema.org/HealthTopicContent"></a> Class: HealthTopicContent <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/HealthTopicContent)</small>

[[HealthTopicContent]] is [[WebContent]] that is about some aspect of a health topic, e.g. a condition, its symptoms or treatments. Such content may be comprised of several parts or sections and use different types of media. Multiple instances of [[WebContent]] (and hence [[HealthTopicContent]]) can be related using [[hasPart]] / [[isPartOf]] where there is some kind of content hierarchy, and their content described with [[about]] and [[mentions]] e.g. building upon the existing [[MedicalCondition]] vocabulary. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FHomeAndConstructionBusiness" title="http://schema.org/HomeAndConstructionBusiness"></a> Class: HomeAndConstructionBusiness <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/HomeAndConstructionBusiness)</small>

A construction business.\n\nA HomeAndConstructionBusiness is a [[LocalBusiness]] that provides services around homes and buildings.\n\nAs a [[LocalBusiness]] it can be described as a [[provider]] of one or more [[Service]]\(s).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

This URL should conform to the particular requirements of digital links. The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FHotel" title="http://schema.org/Hotel"></a> Class: Hotel <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Hotel)</small>

A hotel is an establishment that provides lodging paid on a short-term basis (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel). <br /><br /> See also the <a href="/docs/hotels.html">dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations</a>. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

#### Properties from Thing

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FHotelRoom" title="http://schema.org/HotelRoom"></a> Class: HotelRoom <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/HotelRoom)</small>

A hotel room is a single room in a hotel. <br /><br /> See also the <a href="/docs/hotels.html">dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations</a>. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FHouse" title="http://schema.org/House"></a> Class: House <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/House)</small>

A house is a building or structure that has the ability to be occupied for habitation by humans or other creatures (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House">http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House</a>).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FHowTo" title="http://schema.org/HowTo"></a> Class: HowTo <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/HowTo)</small>

Instructions that explain how to achieve a result by performing a sequence of steps.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FHowToDirection" title="http://schema.org/HowToDirection"></a> Class: HowToDirection <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/HowToDirection)</small>

A direction indicating a single action to do in the instructions for how to achieve a result.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FHowToSection" title="http://schema.org/HowToSection"></a> Class: HowToSection <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/HowToSection)</small>

A sub-grouping of steps in the instructions for how to achieve a result (e.g. steps for making a pie crust within a pie recipe).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. An explanation in the instructions for how to achieve a result. It provides supplementary information about a technique, supply, author's preference, etc. It can explain what could be done, or what should not be done, but doesn't specify what should be done (see HowToDirection).

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FHyperToc" title="http://schema.org/HyperToc"></a> Class: HyperToc <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/HyperToc)</small>

A HyperToc represents a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects, such as [[VideoObject]], [[AudioObject]]. Items in the table of contents are indicated using the [[tocEntry]] property, and typed [[HyperTocEntry]]. For cases where the same larger work is split into multiple files, [[associatedMedia]] can be used on individual [[HyperTocEntry]] items.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FHyperTocEntry" title="http://schema.org/HyperTocEntry"></a> Class: HyperTocEntry <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/HyperTocEntry)</small>

A HyperToEntry is an item within a [[HyperToc]], which represents a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects, such as [[VideoObject]], [[AudioObject]]. The media object itself is indicated using [[associatedMedia]]. Each section of interest within that content can be described with a [[HyperTocEntry]], with associated [[startOffset]] and [[endOffset]]. When several entries are all from the same file, [[associatedMedia]] is used on the overarching [[HyperTocEntry]]; if the content has been split into multiple files, they can be referenced using [[associatedMedia]] on each [[HyperTocEntry]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FIPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration" title="http://schema.org/IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration"></a> Class: IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration)</small>

<a href="https://www.iptc.org/">IPTC</a> "Digital Source" codes for use with the [[digitalSourceType]] property, providing information about the source for a digital media object. In general these codes are not declared here to be mutually exclusive, although some combinations would be contradictory if applied simultaneously, or might be considered mutually incompatible by upstream maintainers of the definitions. See the IPTC <a href="https://www.iptc.org/std/photometadata/documentation/userguide/">documentation</a> for <a href="https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/">detailed definitions</a> of all terms.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FImageObjectSnapshot" title="http://schema.org/ImageObjectSnapshot"></a> Class: ImageObjectSnapshot <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ImageObjectSnapshot)</small>

A specific and exact (byte-for-byte) version of an [[ImageObject]]. Two byte-for-byte identical files, for the purposes of this type, considered identical. If they have different embedded metadata (e.g. XMP, EXIF) the files will differ. Different external facts about the files, e.g. creator or dateCreated that aren't represented in their actual content, do not affect this notion of identity.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FfloorLevel" title="http://schema.org/floorLevel">floorLevel</a> | No | The floor level for an [[Accommodation]] in a multi-storey building. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FIndividualProduct" title="http://schema.org/IndividualProduct"></a> Class: IndividualProduct <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/IndividualProduct)</small>

A single, identifiable product instance (e.g. a laptop with a particular serial number).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin14" title="http://schema.org/gtin14">gtin14</a> | No | The GTIN-14 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin8" title="http://schema.org/gtin8">gtin8</a> | No | The GTIN-8 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This code is also known as EAN/UCC-8 or 8-digit EAN. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasCertification" title="http://schema.org/hasCertification">hasCertification</a> | No | Certification information about a product, organization, service, place, or person. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCertification" title="http://schema.org/Certification">Certification</a> |  |

The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasMeasurement" title="http://schema.org/hasMeasurement">hasMeasurement</a> | No | A measurement of an item, For example, the inseam of pants, the wheel size of a bicycle, the gauge of a screw, or the carbon footprint measured for certification by an authority. Usually an exact measurement, but can also be a range of measurements for adjustable products, for example belts and ski bindings. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasMerchantReturnPolicy" title="http://schema.org/hasMerchantReturnPolicy">hasMerchantReturnPolicy</a> | No | Specifies a MerchantReturnPolicy that may be applicable. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMerchantReturnPolicy" title="http://schema.org/MerchantReturnPolicy">MerchantReturnPolicy</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fheight" title="http://schema.org/height">height</a> | No | The height of the item. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDistance" title="http://schema.org/Distance">Distance</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FinProductGroupWithID" title="http://schema.org/inProductGroupWithID">inProductGroupWithID</a> | No | Indicates the [[productGroupID]] for a [[ProductGroup]] that this product [[isVariantOf]].  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FisConsumableFor" title="http://schema.org/isConsumableFor">isConsumableFor</a> | No | A pointer to another product (or multiple products) for which this product is a consumable. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProduct" title="http://schema.org/Product">Product</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FisRelatedTo" title="http://schema.org/isRelatedTo">isRelatedTo</a> | No | A pointer to another, somehow related product (or multiple products). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProduct" title="http://schema.org/Product">Product</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FService" title="http://schema.org/Service">Service</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FisSimilarTo" title="http://schema.org/isSimilarTo">isSimilarTo</a> | No | A pointer to another, functionally similar product (or multiple products). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProduct" title="http://schema.org/Product">Product</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FService" title="http://schema.org/Service">Service</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FisVariantOf" title="http://schema.org/isVariantOf">isVariantOf</a> | No | Indicates the kind of product that this is a variant of. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmanufacturer" title="http://schema.org/manufacturer">manufacturer</a> | No | The manufacturer of the product. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmobileUrl" title="http://schema.org/mobileUrl">mobileUrl</a> | No | The [[mobileUrl]] property is provided for specific situations in which data consumers need to determine whether one of several provided URLs is a dedicated 'mobile site'. The general trend in web technology is towards [responsive design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsive_web_design) in which content can be flexibly adapted to a wide range of browsing environments. Pages and sites referenced with the long-established [[url]] property should ideally also be usable on a wide variety of devices, including mobile phones. In most cases, it would be pointless and counter productive to attempt to update all [[url]] markup to use [[mobileUrl]] for more mobile-oriented pages. The property is intended for the case when items (primarily [[Product]] and [[Offer]]) have extra URLs hosted on an additional "mobile site" alongside the main one. It should not be taken as an endorsement of this publication style.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

It is recommended to additionally provide strong product identifiers via the gtin8/gtin13/gtin14 and mpn properties. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProductModel" title="http://schema.org/ProductModel">ProductModel</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmpn" title="http://schema.org/mpn">mpn</a> | No | The Manufacturer Part Number (MPN) of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

For symmetry In the case of a [[Review]], the property describes the [[itemReviewed]] from the perspective of the review; in the case of a [[Product]], the product itself is being described. Since product descriptions tend to emphasise positive claims, it may be relatively unusual to find [[negativeNotes]] used in this way. Nevertheless for the sake of symmetry, [[negativeNotes]] can be used on [[Product]]. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Foffers" title="http://schema.org/offers">offers</a> | No | An offer to provide this item&#x2014;for example, an offer to sell a product, rent the DVD of a movie, perform a service, or give away tickets to an event. While this property is listed as expected on a number of common types, it can be used in others. In that case, using a second type, such as Product or a subtype of Product, can clarify the nature of the offer.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDemand" title="http://schema.org/Demand">Demand</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOffer" title="http://schema.org/Offer">Offer</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fpattern" title="http://schema.org/pattern">pattern</a> | No | A pattern that something has, for example 'polka dot', 'striped', 'Canadian flag'. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpositiveNotes" title="http://schema.org/positiveNotes">positiveNotes</a> | No | Provides positive considerations regarding something, for example product highlights or (alongside [[negativeNotes]]) pro/con lists for reviews. The property values can be expressed either as unstructured text (repeated as necessary), or if ordered, as a list (in which case the most positive is at the beginning of the list). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FItemList" title="http://schema.org/ItemList">ItemList</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FListItem" title="http://schema.org/ListItem">ListItem</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FWebContent" title="http://schema.org/WebContent">WebContent</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpurchaseDate" title="http://schema.org/purchaseDate">purchaseDate</a> | No | The date the item, e.g. vehicle, was purchased by the current owner. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDate" title="http://schema.org/Date">Date</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FreleaseDate" title="http://schema.org/releaseDate">releaseDate</a> | No | The release date of a product or product model. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FInfectiousDisease" title="http://schema.org/InfectiousDisease"></a> Class: InfectiousDisease <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/InfectiousDisease)</small>

An infectious disease is a clinically evident human disease resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents, like pathogenic viruses, pathogenic bacteria, fungi, protozoa, multicellular parasites, and prions. To be considered an infectious disease, such pathogens are known to be able to cause this disease.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FInvoice" title="http://schema.org/Invoice"></a> Class: Invoice <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Invoice)</small>

A statement of the money due for goods or services; a bill.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fspeakable" title="http://schema.org/speakable">speakable</a> | No | Indicates sections of a Web page that are particularly 'speakable' in the sense of being highlighted as being especially appropriate for text-to-speech conversion. Other sections of a page may also be usefully spoken in particular circumstances; the 'speakable' property serves to indicate the parts most likely to be generally useful for speech. The *speakable* property can be repeated an arbitrary number of times, with three kinds of possible 'content-locator' values: 1.) *id-value* URL references - uses *id-value* of an element in the page being annotated. The simplest use of *speakable* has (potentially relative) URL values, referencing identified sections of the document concerned. 2.) CSS Selectors - addresses content in the annotated page, e.g. via class attribute. Use the [[cssSelector]] property. 3.) XPaths - addresses content via XPaths (assuming an XML view of the content). Use the [[xpath]] property. For more sophisticated markup of speakable sections beyond simple ID references, either CSS selectors or XPath expressions to pick out document section(s) as speakable. For this we define a supporting type, [[SpeakableSpecification]] which is defined to be a possible value of the *speakable* property.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSpeakableSpecification" title="http://schema.org/SpeakableSpecification">SpeakableSpecification</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fspecialty" title="http://schema.org/specialty">specialty</a> | No | One of the domain specialities to which this web page's content applies. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSpecialty" title="http://schema.org/Specialty">Specialty</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FJobPosting" title="http://schema.org/JobPosting"></a> Class: JobPosting <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/JobPosting)</small>

A listing that describes a job opening in a certain organization.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FJoinAction" title="http://schema.org/JoinAction"></a> Class: JoinAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/JoinAction)</small>

An agent joins an event/group with participants/friends at a location.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, JoinAction refers to joining a group/team of people.\n* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be receiving updates.\n* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be polling for updates.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLandform" title="http://schema.org/Landform"></a> Class: Landform <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Landform)</small>

A landform or physical feature. Landform elements include mountains, plains, lakes, rivers, seascape and oceanic waterbody interface features such as bays, peninsulas, seas and so forth, including sub-aqueous terrain features such as submersed mountain ranges, volcanoes, and the great ocean basins.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLanguage" title="http://schema.org/Language"></a> Class: Language <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Language)</small>

Natural languages such as Spanish, Tamil, Hindi, English, etc. Formal language code tags expressed in [BCP 47](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) can be used via the [[alternateName]] property. The Language type previously also covered programming languages such as Scheme and Lisp, which are now best represented using [[ComputerLanguage]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLearningResource" title="http://schema.org/LearningResource"></a> Class: LearningResource <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/LearningResource)</small>

The LearningResource type can be used to indicate [[CreativeWork]]s (whether physical or digital) that have a particular and explicit orientation towards learning, education, skill acquisition, and other educational purposes. [[LearningResource]] is expected to be used as an addition to a primary type such as [[Book]], [[VideoObject]], [[Product]] etc. [[EducationEvent]] serves a similar purpose for event-like things (e.g. a [[Trip]]). A [[LearningResource]] may be created as a result of an [[EducationEvent]], for example by recording one.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

For something that can be commercially licensed, usageInfo can provide detailed, resource-specific information about licensing options. This property can be used alongside the license property which indicates license(s) applicable to some piece of content. The usageInfo property can provide information about other licensing options, e.g. acquiring commercial usage rights for an image that is also available under non-commercial creative commons licenses. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCreativeWork" title="http://schema.org/CreativeWork">CreativeWork</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegalService" title="http://schema.org/LegalService"></a> Class: LegalService <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/LegalService)</small>

A LegalService is a business that provides legally-oriented services, advice and representation, e.g. law firms.\n\nAs a [[LocalBusiness]] it can be described as a [[provider]] of one or more [[Service]]\(s).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fjurisdiction" title="http://schema.org/jurisdiction">jurisdiction</a> | No | Indicates a legal jurisdiction, e.g. of some legislation, or where some government service is based. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FAdministrativeArea" title="http://schema.org/AdministrativeArea">AdministrativeArea</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationAmends" title="http://schema.org/legislationAmends">legislationAmends</a> | No | Another legislation that this legislation amends, introducing legal changes. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationApplies" title="http://schema.org/legislationApplies">legislationApplies</a> | No | Indicates that this legislation (or part of a legislation) somehow transfers another legislation in a different legislative context. This is an informative link, and it has no legal value. For legally-binding links of transposition, use the <a href="/legislationTransposes">legislationTransposes</a> property. For example an informative consolidated law of a European Union's member state "applies" the consolidated version of the European Directive implemented in it. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationChanges" title="http://schema.org/legislationChanges">legislationChanges</a> | No | Another legislation that this legislation changes. This encompasses the notions of amendment, replacement, correction, repeal, or other types of change. This may be a direct change (textual or non-textual amendment) or a consequential or indirect change. The property is to be used to express the existence of a change relationship between two acts rather than the existence of a consolidated version of the text that shows the result of the change. For consolidation relationships, use the <a href="/legislationConsolidates">legislationConsolidates</a> property. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationCommences" title="http://schema.org/legislationCommences">legislationCommences</a> | No | Another legislation that this one sets into force. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationConsolidates" title="http://schema.org/legislationConsolidates">legislationConsolidates</a> | No | Indicates another legislation taken into account in this consolidated legislation (which is usually the product of an editorial process that revises the legislation). This property should be used multiple times to refer to both the original version or the previous consolidated version, and to the legislations making the change. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationCorrects" title="http://schema.org/legislationCorrects">legislationCorrects</a> | No | Another legislation in which this one introduces textual changes, like correction of spelling mistakes, with no legal impact (for modifications that have legal impact, use <a href="/legislationAmends">legislationAmends</a>). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationCountersignedBy" title="http://schema.org/legislationCountersignedBy">legislationCountersignedBy</a> | No | The person or organization that countersigned the legislation. Depending on the legal context, a countersignature can indicate that the signed authority undertakes to assume responsibility for texts emanating from a person who is inviolable and irresponsible, (for example a King, Grand Duc or President), or that the authority is in charge of the implementation of the text. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationDate" title="http://schema.org/legislationDate">legislationDate</a> | No | The date of adoption or signature of the legislation. This is the date at which the text is officially aknowledged to be a legislation, even though it might not even be published or in force. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDate" title="http://schema.org/Date">Date</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationDateOfApplicability" title="http://schema.org/legislationDateOfApplicability">legislationDateOfApplicability</a> | No | The date at which the Legislation becomes applicable. This can sometimes be distinct from the date of entry into force : a text may come in force today, and state it will become applicable in 3 months. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDate" title="http://schema.org/Date">Date</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationDateVersion" title="http://schema.org/legislationDateVersion">legislationDateVersion</a> | No | The point-in-time at which the provided description of the legislation is valid (e.g.: when looking at the law on the 2016-04-07 (= dateVersion), I get the consolidation of 2015-04-12 of the "National Insurance Contributions Act 2015") | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDate" title="http://schema.org/Date">Date</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationEnsuresImplementationOf" title="http://schema.org/legislationEnsuresImplementationOf">legislationEnsuresImplementationOf</a> | No | Indicates that this Legislation ensures the implementation of another Legislation, for example by modifying national legislations so that they do not contradict to an EU regulation or decision. This implies a legal meaning. Transpositions of EU Directive should be captured with <a href="/legislationTransposes">legislationTransposes</a>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationIdentifier" title="http://schema.org/legislationIdentifier">legislationIdentifier</a> | No | An identifier for the legislation. This can be either a string-based identifier, like the CELEX at EU level or the NOR in France, or a web-based, URL/URI identifier, like an ELI (European Legislation Identifier) or an URN-Lex. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationJurisdiction" title="http://schema.org/legislationJurisdiction">legislationJurisdiction</a> | No | The jurisdiction from which the legislation originates. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FAdministrativeArea" title="http://schema.org/AdministrativeArea">AdministrativeArea</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationLegalForce" title="http://schema.org/legislationLegalForce">legislationLegalForce</a> | No | Whether the legislation is currently in force, not in force, or partially in force. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegalForceStatus" title="http://schema.org/LegalForceStatus">LegalForceStatus</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationPassedBy" title="http://schema.org/legislationPassedBy">legislationPassedBy</a> | No | The person or organization that originally passed or made the law: typically parliament (for primary legislation) or government (for secondary legislation). This indicates the "legal author" of the law, as opposed to its physical author. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationRepeals" title="http://schema.org/legislationRepeals">legislationRepeals</a> | No | Another legislation that this legislation repeals (cancels, abrogates). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationResponsible" title="http://schema.org/legislationResponsible">legislationResponsible</a> | No | An individual or organization that has some kind of responsibility for the legislation. Typically the ministry who is/was in charge of elaborating the legislation, or the adressee for potential questions about the legislation once it is published. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationTransposes" title="http://schema.org/legislationTransposes">legislationTransposes</a> | No | Indicates that this legislation (or part of legislation) fulfills the objectives set by another legislation, by passing appropriate implementation measures. Typically, some legislations of European Union's member states or regions transpose European Directives. This indicates a legally binding link between the 2 legislations. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationType" title="http://schema.org/legislationType">legislationType</a> | No | The type of the legislation. Examples of values are "law", "act", "directive", "decree", "regulation", "statutory instrument", "loi organique", "règlement grand-ducal", etc., depending on the country. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCategoryCode" title="http://schema.org/CategoryCode">CategoryCode</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislationObject" title="http://schema.org/LegislationObject"></a> Class: LegislationObject <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/LegislationObject)</small>

A specific object or file containing a Legislation. Note that the same Legislation can be published in multiple files. For example, a digitally signed PDF, a plain PDF and an HTML version.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Typically a digitally signed PDF have a "stronger" legal value than the HTML file of the same act. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegalValueLevel" title="http://schema.org/LegalValueLevel">LegalValueLevel</a> |  |

This can sometimes be distinct from the date of entry into force : a text may come in force today, and state it will become applicable in 3 months. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDate" title="http://schema.org/Date">Date</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationDateVersion" title="http://schema.org/legislationDateVersion">legislationDateVersion</a> | No | The point-in-time at which the provided description of the legislation is valid (e.g.: when looking at the law on the 2016-04-07 (= dateVersion), I get the consolidation of 2015-04-12 of the "National Insurance Contributions Act 2015") | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDate" title="http://schema.org/Date">Date</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationEnsuresImplementationOf" title="http://schema.org/legislationEnsuresImplementationOf">legislationEnsuresImplementationOf</a> | No | Indicates that this Legislation ensures the implementation of another Legislation, for example by modifying national legislations so that they do not contradict to an EU regulation or decision. This implies a legal meaning. Transpositions of EU Directive should be captured with <a href="/legislationTransposes">legislationTransposes</a>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationIdentifier" title="http://schema.org/legislationIdentifier">legislationIdentifier</a> | No | An identifier for the legislation. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationJurisdiction" title="http://schema.org/legislationJurisdiction">legislationJurisdiction</a> | No | The jurisdiction from which the legislation originates. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FAdministrativeArea" title="http://schema.org/AdministrativeArea">AdministrativeArea</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationLegalForce" title="http://schema.org/legislationLegalForce">legislationLegalForce</a> | No | Whether the legislation is currently in force, not in force, or partially in force. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegalForceStatus" title="http://schema.org/LegalForceStatus">LegalForceStatus</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationPassedBy" title="http://schema.org/legislationPassedBy">legislationPassedBy</a> | No | The person or organization that originally passed or made the law: typically parliament (for primary legislation) or government (for secondary legislation). This indicates the "legal author" of the law, as opposed to its physical author. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationRepeals" title="http://schema.org/legislationRepeals">legislationRepeals</a> | No | Another legislation that this legislation repeals (cancels, abrogates). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationResponsible" title="http://schema.org/legislationResponsible">legislationResponsible</a> | No | An individual or organization that has some kind of responsibility for the legislation. Typically the ministry who is/was in charge of elaborating the legislation, or the adressee for potential questions about the legislation once it is published. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationTransposes" title="http://schema.org/legislationTransposes">legislationTransposes</a> | No | Indicates that this legislation (or part of legislation) fulfills the objectives set by another legislation, by passing appropriate implementation measures. Typically, some legislations of European Union's member states or regions transpose European Directives. This indicates a legally binding link between the 2 legislations. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLegislation" title="http://schema.org/Legislation">Legislation</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FlegislationType" title="http://schema.org/legislationType">legislationType</a> | No | The type of the legislation. Examples of values are "law", "act", "directive", "decree", "regulation", "statutory instrument", "loi organique", "règlement grand-ducal", etc., depending on the country. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCategoryCode" title="http://schema.org/CategoryCode">CategoryCode</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLinkRole" title="http://schema.org/LinkRole"></a> Class: LinkRole <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/LinkRole)</small>

A Role that represents a Web link, e.g. as expressed via the 'url' property. Its linkRelationship property can indicate URL-based and plain textual link types, e.g. those in IANA link registry or others such as 'amphtml'. This structure provides a placeholder where details from HTML's link element can be represented outside of HTML, e.g. in JSON-LD feeds.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLiveBlogPosting" title="http://schema.org/LiveBlogPosting"></a> Class: LiveBlogPosting <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/LiveBlogPosting)</small>

A [[LiveBlogPosting]] is a [[BlogPosting]] intended to provide a rolling textual coverage of an ongoing event through continuous updates.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

The LiveBlogPosting may also be created before coverage begins. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDateTime" title="http://schema.org/DateTime">DateTime</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLoanOrCredit" title="http://schema.org/LoanOrCredit"></a> Class: LoanOrCredit <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/LoanOrCredit)</small>

A financial product for the loaning of an amount of money, or line of credit, under agreed terms and charges.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FLocalBusiness" title="http://schema.org/LocalBusiness"></a> Class: LocalBusiness <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/LocalBusiness)</small>

A particular physical business or branch of an organization. Examples of LocalBusiness include a restaurant, a particular branch of a restaurant chain, a branch of a bank, a medical practice, a club, a bowling alley, etc.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The identifier should be in the `XXXX:YYYYYY:ZZZ` or `XXXX:YYYYYY`format. Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| N/A | N/A |

This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMediaManipulationRatingEnumeration" title="http://schema.org/MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration"></a> Class: MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration)</small>

 Codes for use with the [[mediaAuthenticityCategory]] property, indicating the authenticity of a media object (in the context of how it was published or shared). In general these codes are not mutually exclusive, although some combinations (such as 'original' versus 'transformed', 'edited' and 'staged') would be contradictory if applied in the same [[MediaReview]]. Note that the application of these codes is with regard to a piece of media shared or published in a particular context.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMediaObject" title="http://schema.org/MediaObject"></a> Class: MediaObject <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MediaObject)</small>

A media object, such as an image, video, audio, or text object embedded in a web page or a downloadable dataset i.e. DataDownload. Note that a creative work may have many media objects associated with it on the same web page. For example, a page about a single song (MusicRecording) may have a music video (VideoObject), and a high and low bandwidth audio stream (2 AudioObject's).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMediaReview" title="http://schema.org/MediaReview"></a> Class: MediaReview <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MediaReview)</small>

A [[MediaReview]] is a more specialized form of Review dedicated to the evaluation of media content online, typically in the context of fact-checking and misinformation. For more general reviews of media in the broader sense, use [[UserReview]], [[CriticReview]] or other [[Review]] types. This definition is a work in progress. While the [[MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration]] list reflects significant community review amongst fact-checkers and others working to combat misinformation, the specific structures for representing media objects, their versions and publication context, are still evolving. Similarly, best practices for the relationship between [[MediaReview]] and [[ClaimReview]] markup have not yet been finalized.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

It is common for distributions of software and data to be based on "upstream" sources. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMediaReviewItem" title="http://schema.org/MediaReviewItem"></a> Class: MediaReviewItem <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MediaReviewItem)</small>

Represents an item or group of closely related items treated as a unit for the sake of evaluation in a [[MediaReview]]. Authorship etc. apply to the items rather than to the curation/grouping or reviewing party.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. In the case of text values, the class label should follow the schema.org <a href="https://schema.org/docs/styleguide.html">style guide</a>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMedicalCause" title="http://schema.org/MedicalCause"></a> Class: MedicalCause <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MedicalCause)</small>

The causative agent(s) that are responsible for the pathophysiologic process that eventually results in a medical condition, symptom or sign. In this schema, unless otherwise specified this is meant to be the proximate cause of the medical condition, symptom or sign. The proximate cause is defined as the causative agent that most directly results in the medical condition, symptom or sign. For example, the HIV virus could be considered a cause of AIDS. Or in a diagnostic context, if a patient fell and sustained a hip fracture and two days later sustained a pulmonary embolism which eventuated in a cardiac arrest, the cause of the cardiac arrest (the proximate cause) would be the pulmonary embolism and not the fall. Medical causes can include cardiovascular, chemical, dermatologic, endocrine, environmental, gastroenterologic, genetic, hematologic, gynecologic, iatrogenic, infectious, musculoskeletal, neurologic, nutritional, obstetric, oncologic, otolaryngologic, pharmacologic, psychiatric, pulmonary, renal, rheumatologic, toxic, traumatic, or urologic causes; medical conditions can be causes as well.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. In the case of text values, the class label should follow the schema.org <a href="https://schema.org/docs/styleguide.html">style guide</a>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fdescription" title="http://schema.org/description">description</a> | No | A description of the item. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FTextObject" title="http://schema.org/TextObject">TextObject</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMedicalContraindication" title="http://schema.org/MedicalContraindication"></a> Class: MedicalContraindication <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MedicalContraindication)</small>

A condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a certain medical therapy. Contraindications can be absolute (there are no reasonable circumstances for undertaking a course of action) or relative (the patient is at higher risk of complications, but these risks may be outweighed by other considerations or mitigated by other measures).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMedicalGuideline" title="http://schema.org/MedicalGuideline"></a> Class: MedicalGuideline <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MedicalGuideline)</small>

Any recommendation made by a standard society (e.g. ACC/AHA) or consensus statement that denotes how to diagnose and treat a particular condition. Note: this type should be used to tag the actual guideline recommendation; if the guideline recommendation occurs in a larger scholarly article, use MedicalScholarlyArticle to tag the overall article, not this type. Note also: the organization making the recommendation should be captured in the recognizingAuthority base property of MedicalEntity.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMedicalObservationalStudy" title="http://schema.org/MedicalObservationalStudy"></a> Class: MedicalObservationalStudy <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MedicalObservationalStudy)</small>

An observational study is a type of medical study that attempts to infer the possible effect of a treatment through observation of a cohort of subjects over a period of time. In an observational study, the assignment of subjects into treatment groups versus control groups is outside the control of the investigator. This is in contrast with controlled studies, such as the randomized controlled trials represented by MedicalTrial, where each subject is randomly assigned to a treatment group or a control group before the start of the treatment.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpageEnd" title="http://schema.org/pageEnd">pageEnd</a> | No | The page on which the work ends; for example "138" or "xvi". | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FInteger" title="http://schema.org/Integer">Integer</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpageStart" title="http://schema.org/pageStart">pageStart</a> | No | The page on which the work starts; for example "135" or "xiii". | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FInteger" title="http://schema.org/Integer">Integer</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fpagination" title="http://schema.org/pagination">pagination</a> | No | Any description of pages that is not separated into pageStart and pageEnd; for example, "1-6, 9, 55" or "10-12, 46-49". | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fspeakable" title="http://schema.org/speakable">speakable</a> | No | Indicates sections of a Web page that are particularly 'speakable' in the sense of being highlighted as being especially appropriate for text-to-speech conversion. Other sections of a page may also be usefully spoken in particular circumstances; the 'speakable' property serves to indicate the parts most likely to be generally useful for speech. The *speakable* property can be repeated an arbitrary number of times, with three kinds of possible 'content-locator' values: 1.) *id-value* URL references - uses *id-value* of an element in the page being annotated. The simplest use of *speakable* has (potentially relative) URL values, referencing identified sections of the document concerned. 2.) CSS Selectors - addresses content in the annotated page, e.g. via class attribute. Use the [[cssSelector]] property. 3.) XPaths - addresses content via XPaths (assuming an XML view of the content). Use the [[xpath]] property. For more sophisticated markup of speakable sections beyond simple ID references, either CSS selectors or XPath expressions to pick out document section(s) as speakable. For this we define a supporting type, [[SpeakableSpecification]] which is defined to be a possible value of the *speakable* property.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSpeakableSpecification" title="http://schema.org/SpeakableSpecification">SpeakableSpecification</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FwordCount" title="http://schema.org/wordCount">wordCount</a> | No | The number of words in the text of the CreativeWork such as an Article, Book, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FInteger" title="http://schema.org/Integer">Integer</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMedicalSign" title="http://schema.org/MedicalSign"></a> Class: MedicalSign <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MedicalSign)</small>

Any physical manifestation of a person's medical condition discoverable by objective diagnostic tests or physical examination.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMedicalStudy" title="http://schema.org/MedicalStudy"></a> Class: MedicalStudy <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MedicalStudy)</small>

A medical study is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health, including observational studies and interventional trials and registries, randomized, controlled or not. When the specific type of study is known, use one of the extensions of this type, such as MedicalTrial or MedicalObservationalStudy. Also, note that this type should be used to mark up data that describes the study itself; to tag an article that publishes the results of a study, use MedicalScholarlyArticle. Note: use the code property of MedicalEntity to store study IDs, e.g. clinicaltrials.gov ID.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMedicalTherapy" title="http://schema.org/MedicalTherapy"></a> Class: MedicalTherapy <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MedicalTherapy)</small>

Any medical intervention designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions, including both curative and palliative therapies. Medical therapies are typically processes of care relying upon pharmacotherapy, behavioral therapy, supportive therapy (with fluid or nutrition for example), or detoxification (e.g. hemodialysis) aimed at improving or preventing a health condition.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMedicalTrial" title="http://schema.org/MedicalTrial"></a> Class: MedicalTrial <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MedicalTrial)</small>

A medical trial is a type of medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or medical procedures. In general, medical trials are controlled and subjects are allocated at random to the different treatment and/or control groups.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMemberProgram" title="http://schema.org/MemberProgram"></a> Class: MemberProgram <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MemberProgram)</small>

A MemberProgram defines a loyalty (or membership) program that provides its members with certain benefits, for example better pricing, free shipping or returns, or the ability to earn loyalty points. Member programs may have multiple tiers, for example silver and gold members, each with different benefits.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhostingOrganization" title="http://schema.org/hostingOrganization">hostingOrganization</a> | No | The Organization (airline, travelers' club, retailer, etc.) the membership is made with or which offers the MemberProgram. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMenu" title="http://schema.org/Menu"></a> Class: Menu <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Menu)</small>

A structured representation of food or drink items available from a FoodEstablishment.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| --------- | --------- |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMenuSection" title="http://schema.org/MenuSection"></a> Class: MenuSection <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MenuSection)</small>

A MerchantReturnPolicy provides information about product return policies associated with an [[Organization]], [[Product]], or [[Offer]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMessage" title="http://schema.org/Message"></a> Class: Message <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Message)</small>

A single message from a sender to one or more organizations or people.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMobileApplication" title="http://schema.org/MobileApplication"></a> Class: MobileApplication <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MobileApplication)</small>

A software application designed specifically to work well on a mobile device such as a telephone.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMolecularEntity" title="http://schema.org/MolecularEntity"></a> Class: MolecularEntity <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MolecularEntity)</small>

Any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, ion pair, radical, radical ion, complex, conformer etc., identifiable as a separately distinguishable entity.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMonetaryAmount" title="http://schema.org/MonetaryAmount"></a> Class: MonetaryAmount <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MonetaryAmount)</small>

A monetary value or range. This type can be used to describe an amount of money such as $50 USD, or a range as in describing a bank account being suitable for a balance between £1,000 and £1,000,000 GBP, or the value of a salary, etc. It is recommended to use [[PriceSpecification]] Types to describe the price of an Offer, Invoice, etc.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMortgageLoan" title="http://schema.org/MortgageLoan"></a> Class: MortgageLoan <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MortgageLoan)</small>

A loan in which property or real estate is used as collateral. (A loan securitized against some real estate.)

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMotorcycle" title="http://schema.org/Motorcycle"></a> Class: Motorcycle <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Motorcycle)</small>

A motorcycle or motorbike is a single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin" title="http://schema.org/gtin">gtin</a> | No | A Global Trade Item Number ([GTIN](https://www.gs1.org/standards/id-keys/gtin)). GTINs identify trade items, including products and services, using numeric identification codes. A correct [[gtin]] value should be a valid GTIN, which means that it should be an all-numeric string of either 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits, or a "GS1 Digital Link" URL based on such a string. The numeric component should also have a [valid GS1 check digit](https://www.gs1.org/services/check-digit-calculator) and meet the other rules for valid GTINs. See also [GS1's GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) and [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Trade_Item_Number) for more details. Left-padding of the gtin values is not required or encouraged. The [[gtin]] property generalizes the earlier [[gtin8]], [[gtin12]], [[gtin13]], and [[gtin14]] properties. The GS1 [digital link specifications](https://www.gs1.org/standards/Digital-Link/) expresses GTINs as URLs (URIs, IRIs, etc.). Digital Links should be populated into the [[hasGS1DigitalLink]] attribute. Note also that this is a definition for how to include GTINs in Schema.org data, and not a definition of GTINs in general - see the GS1 documentation for authoritative details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin12" title="http://schema.org/gtin12">gtin12</a> | No | The GTIN-12 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. The GTIN-12 is the 12-digit GS1 Identification Key composed of a U.P.C. Company Prefix, Item Reference, and Check Digit used to identify trade items. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin13" title="http://schema.org/gtin13">gtin13</a> | No | The GTIN-13 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This is equivalent to 13-digit ISBN codes and EAN UCC-13. Former 12-digit UPC codes can be converted into a GTIN-13 code by simply adding a preceding zero. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin14" title="http://schema.org/gtin14">gtin14</a> | No | The GTIN-14 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin8" title="http://schema.org/gtin8">gtin8</a> | No | The GTIN-8 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This code is also known as EAN/UCC-8 or 8-digit EAN. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
