| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasCertification" title="http://schema.org/hasCertification">hasCertification</a> | No | Certification information about a product, organization, service, place, or person. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCertification" title="http://schema.org/Certification">Certification</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasEnergyConsumptionDetails" title="http://schema.org/hasEnergyConsumptionDetails">hasEnergyConsumptionDetails</a> | No | Defines the energy efficiency Category (also known as "class" or "rating") for a product according to an international energy efficiency standard. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FEnergyConsumptionDetails" title="http://schema.org/EnergyConsumptionDetails">EnergyConsumptionDetails</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasGS1DigitalLink" title="http://schema.org/hasGS1DigitalLink">hasGS1DigitalLink</a> | No | The <a href="https://www.gs1.org/standards/gs1-digital-link">GS1 digital link</a> associated with the object. This URL should conform to the particular requirements of digital links. The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmobileUrl" title="http://schema.org/mobileUrl">mobileUrl</a> | No | The [[mobileUrl]] property is provided for specific situations in which data consumers need to determine whether one of several provided URLs is a dedicated 'mobile site'. To discourage over-use, and reflecting intial usecases, the property is expected only on [[Product]] and [[Offer]], rather than [[Thing]]. The general trend in web technology is towards [responsive design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsive_web_design) in which content can be flexibly adapted to a wide range of browsing environments. Pages and sites referenced with the long-established [[url]] property should ideally also be usable on a wide variety of devices, including mobile phones. In most cases, it would be pointless and counter productive to attempt to update all [[url]] markup to use [[mobileUrl]] for more mobile-oriented pages. The property is intended for the case when items (primarily [[Product]] and [[Offer]]) have extra URLs hosted on an additional "mobile site" alongside the main one. It should not be taken as an endorsement of this publication style.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmpn" title="http://schema.org/mpn">mpn</a> | No | The Manufacturer Part Number (MPN) of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMotorizedBicycle" title="http://schema.org/MotorizedBicycle"></a> Class: MotorizedBicycle <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MotorizedBicycle)</small>

A motorized bicycle is a bicycle with an attached motor used to power the vehicle, or to assist with pedaling.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmobileUrl" title="http://schema.org/mobileUrl">mobileUrl</a> | No | The [[mobileUrl]] property is provided for specific situations in which data consumers need to determine whether one of several provided URLs is a dedicated 'mobile site'. The general trend in web technology is towards [responsive design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsive_web_design) in which content can be flexibly adapted to a wide range of browsing environments. Pages and sites referenced with the long-established [[url]] property should ideally also be usable on a wide variety of devices, including mobile phones. In most cases, it would be pointless and counter productive to attempt to update all [[url]] markup to use [[mobileUrl]] for more mobile-oriented pages. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMoveAction" title="http://schema.org/MoveAction"></a> Class: MoveAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MoveAction)</small>

The act of an agent relocating to a place.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[TransferAction]]: Unlike TransferAction, the subject of the move is a living Person or Organization rather than an inanimate object.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMuscle" title="http://schema.org/Muscle"></a> Class: Muscle <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Muscle)</small>

A muscle is an anatomical structure consisting of a contractile form of tissue that animals use to effect movement.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmaintainer" title="http://schema.org/maintainer">maintainer</a> | No | A maintainer of a [[Dataset]], software package ([[SoftwareApplication]]), or other [[Project]]. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMusicGroup" title="http://schema.org/MusicGroup"></a> Class: MusicGroup <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MusicGroup)</small>

A musical group, such as a band, an orchestra, or a choir. Can also be a solo musician.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMusicRecording" title="http://schema.org/MusicRecording"></a> Class: MusicRecording <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MusicRecording)</small>

A music recording (track), usually a single song.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMusicRelease" title="http://schema.org/MusicRelease"></a> Class: MusicRelease <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/MusicRelease)</small>

A MusicRelease is a specific release of a music album.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FtemporalCoverage" title="http://schema.org/temporalCoverage">temporalCoverage</a> | No | The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in [ISO 8601 time interval format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals). Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FNerve" title="http://schema.org/Nerve"></a> Class: Nerve <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Nerve)</small>

A common pathway for the electrochemical nerve impulses that are transmitted along each of the axons.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FNewsArticle" title="http://schema.org/NewsArticle"></a> Class: NewsArticle <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/NewsArticle)</small>

A NewsArticle is an article whose content reports news, or provides background context and supporting materials for understanding the news. A more detailed overview of [schema.org News markup](/docs/news.html) is also available. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Sometimes only a placename is provided. Structured representations of dateline-related information can also be expressed more explicitly using [[locationCreated]] (which represents where a work was created, e.g. where a news report was written). The *speakable* property can be repeated an arbitrary number of times, with three kinds of possible 'content-locator' values: 1.) *id-value* URL references - uses *id-value* of an element in the page being annotated. CSS Selectors - addresses content in the annotated page, e.g. via class attribute. Use the [[cssSelector]] property. 3.) XPaths - addresses content via XPaths (assuming an XML view of the content). Use the [[xpath]] property. For more sophisticated markup of speakable sections beyond simple ID references, either CSS selectors or XPath expressions to pick out document section(s) as speakable. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FNewspaper" title="http://schema.org/Newspaper"></a> Class: Newspaper <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Newspaper)</small>

A publication containing information about varied topics that are pertinent to general information, a geographic area, or a specific subject matter (i.e. business, culture, education). Often published daily.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FNumber" title="http://schema.org/Number"></a> Class: Number <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Number)</small>

Data type: Number.\n\nUsage guidelines:\n\n* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.\n* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FObservation" title="http://schema.org/Observation"></a> Class: Observation <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Observation)</small>

Instances of the class [[Observation]] are used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time. The principal properties of an [[Observation]] are [[observationAbout]], [[measuredProperty]], [[statType]], [[value] and [[observationDate]] and [[measuredProperty]]. Some but not all Observations represent a [[QuantitativeValue]]. Quantitative observations can be about a [[StatisticalVariable]], which is an abstract specification about which we can make observations that are grounded at a particular location and time. Observations can also encode a subset of simple RDF-like statements (its observationAbout, a StatisticalVariable, defining the measuredPoperty; its observationAbout property indicating the entity the statement is about, and [[value]] ) In the context of a quantitative knowledge graph, typical properties could include [[measuredProperty]], [[observationAbout]], [[observationDate]], [[value]], [[unitCode]], [[unitText]], [[measurementMethod]]. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Often but not necessarily each [[variableMeasured]] will have an explicit representation as (or mapping to) an property such as those defined in Schema.org, or other RDF vocabularies and "knowledge graphs". ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOffer" title="http://schema.org/Offer"></a> Class: Offer <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Offer)</small>

An offer to transfer some rights to an item or to provide a service — for example, an offer to sell tickets to an event, to rent the DVD of a movie, to stream a TV show over the internet, to repair a motorcycle, or to loan a book.\n\nNote: As the [[businessFunction]] property, which identifies the form of offer (e.g. sell, lease, repair, dispose), defaults to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell; an Offer without a defined businessFunction value can be assumed to be an offer to sell.\n\nFor [GTIN](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin)-related fields, see [Check Digit calculator](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/support/check_digit_calculator) and [validation guide](http://www.gs1us.org/resources/standards/gtin-validation-guide) from [GS1](http://www.gs1.org/).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOfferCatalog" title="http://schema.org/OfferCatalog"></a> Class: OfferCatalog <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/OfferCatalog)</small>

An OfferCatalog is an ItemList that contains related Offers and/or further OfferCatalogs that are offeredBy the same provider.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOfferForLease" title="http://schema.org/OfferForLease"></a> Class: OfferForLease <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/OfferForLease)</small>

An [[OfferForLease]] in Schema.org represents an [[Offer]] to lease out something, i.e. an [[Offer]] whose [[businessFunction]] is [lease out](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#LeaseOut.). See [Good Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoodRelations) for background on the underlying concepts. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOfferForPurchase" title="http://schema.org/OfferForPurchase"></a> Class: OfferForPurchase <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/OfferForPurchase)</small>

An [[OfferForPurchase]] in Schema.org represents an [[Offer]] to sell something, i.e. an [[Offer]] whose [[businessFunction]] is [sell](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell.). See [Good Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoodRelations) for background on the underlying concepts. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FeligibleDuration" title="http://schema.org/eligibleDuration">eligibleDuration</a> | No | The duration for which the given offer is valid. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin" title="http://schema.org/gtin">gtin</a> | No | A Global Trade Item Number ([GTIN](https://www.gs1.org/standards/id-keys/gtin)). GTINs identify trade items, including products and services, using numeric identification codes. The numeric component should also have a [valid GS1 check digit](https://www.gs1.org/services/check-digit-calculator) and meet the other rules for valid GTINs. See also [GS1's GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) and [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Trade_Item_Number) for more details. Left-padding of the gtin values is not required or encouraged. The [[gtin]] property generalizes the earlier [[gtin8]], [[gtin12]], [[gtin13]], and [[gtin14]] properties. The GS1 [digital link specifications](https://www.gs1.org/standards/Digital-Link/) expresses GTINs as URLs (URIs, IRIs, etc.). Digital Links should be populated into the [[hasGS1DigitalLink]] attribute. Note also that this is a definition for how to include GTINs in Schema.org data, and not a definition of GTINs in general - see the GS1 documentation for authoritative details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin12" title="http://schema.org/gtin12">gtin12</a> | No | The GTIN-12 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasGS1DigitalLink" title="http://schema.org/hasGS1DigitalLink">hasGS1DigitalLink</a> | No | The <a href="https://www.gs1.org/standards/gs1-digital-link">GS1 digital link</a> associated with the object. This URL should conform to the particular requirements of digital links. The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

Usually an exact measurement, but can also be a range of measurements for adjustable products, for example belts and ski bindings. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FleaseLength" title="http://schema.org/leaseLength">leaseLength</a> | No | Length of the lease for some [[Accommodation]], either particular to some [[Offer]] or in some cases intrinsic to the property. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDuration" title="http://schema.org/Duration">Duration</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmobileUrl" title="http://schema.org/mobileUrl">mobileUrl</a> | No | The [[mobileUrl]] property is provided for specific situations in which data consumers need to determine whether one of several provided URLs is a dedicated 'mobile site'. To discourage over-use, and reflecting intial usecases, the property is expected only on [[Product]] and [[Offer]], rather than [[Thing]]. The general trend in web technology is towards [responsive design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsive_web_design) in which content can be flexibly adapted to a wide range of browsing environments. Pages and sites referenced with the long-established [[url]] property should ideally also be usable on a wide variety of devices, including mobile phones. In most cases, it would be pointless and counter productive to attempt to update all [[url]] markup to use [[mobileUrl]] for more mobile-oriented pages. (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.\n* Note that both [RDFa](http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml-rdfa-primer/#using-the-content-attribute) and Microdata syntax allow the use of a "content=" attribute for publishing simple machine-readable values alongside more human-friendly formatting.\n* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FNumber" title="http://schema.org/Number">Number</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceCurrency" title="http://schema.org/priceCurrency">priceCurrency</a> | No | The currency of the price, or a price component when attached to [[PriceSpecification]] and its subtypes.\n\nUse standard formats: [ISO 4217 currency format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217), e.g. "USD"; [Ticker symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cryptocurrencies) for cryptocurrencies, e.g. "BTC"; well known names for [Local Exchange Trading Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_exchange_trading_system) (LETS) and other currency types, e.g. "Ithaca HOUR". | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceSpecification" title="http://schema.org/priceSpecification">priceSpecification</a> | No | One or more detailed price specifications, indicating the unit price and delivery or payment charges. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPriceSpecification" title="http://schema.org/PriceSpecification">PriceSpecification</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOfferShippingDetails" title="http://schema.org/OfferShippingDetails"></a> Class: OfferShippingDetails <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/OfferShippingDetails)</small>

OfferShippingDetails represents information about shipping destinations. Multiple of these entities can be used to represent different shipping rates for different destinations: One entity for Alaska/Hawaii. A different one for continental US. A different one for all France. Multiple of these entities can be used to represent different shipping costs and delivery times. Two entities that are identical but differ in rate and time: E.g. Cheaper and slower: $5 in 5-7 days or Fast and expensive: $15 in 1-2 days.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOnDemandEvent" title="http://schema.org/OnDemandEvent"></a> Class: OnDemandEvent <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/OnDemandEvent)</small>

A publication event, e.g. catch-up TV or radio podcast, during which a program is available on-demand.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOnlineBusiness" title="http://schema.org/OnlineBusiness"></a> Class: OnlineBusiness <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/OnlineBusiness)</small>

A particular online business, either standalone or the online part of a broader organization. Examples include an eCommerce site, an online travel booking site, an online learning site, an online logistics and shipping provider, an online (virtual) doctor, etc.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. #### Properties from Thing

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOpeningHoursSpecification" title="http://schema.org/OpeningHoursSpecification"></a> Class: OpeningHoursSpecification <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/OpeningHoursSpecification)</small>

A structured value providing information about the opening hours of a place or a certain service inside a place.\n\n The place is __open__ if the [[opens]] property is specified, and __closed__ otherwise.\n\nIf the value for the [[closes]] property is less than the value for the [[opens]] property then the hour range is assumed to span over the next day. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOpinionNewsArticle" title="http://schema.org/OpinionNewsArticle"></a> Class: OpinionNewsArticle <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/OpinionNewsArticle)</small>

An [[OpinionNewsArticle]] is a [[NewsArticle]] that primarily expresses opinions rather than journalistic reporting of news and events. For example, a [[NewsArticle]] consisting of a column or [[Blog]]/[[BlogPosting]] entry in the Opinions section of a news publication. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrder" title="http://schema.org/Order"></a> Class: Order <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Order)</small>

An order is a confirmation of a transaction (a receipt), which can contain multiple line items, each represented by an Offer that has been accepted by the customer.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The identifier should be in the `XXXX:YYYYYY:ZZZ` or `XXXX:YYYYYY`format. Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPalliativeProcedure" title="http://schema.org/PalliativeProcedure"></a> Class: PalliativeProcedure <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PalliativeProcedure)</small>

A medical procedure intended primarily for palliative purposes, aimed at relieving the symptoms of an underlying health condition.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FopeningHours" title="http://schema.org/openingHours">openingHours</a> | No | The general opening hours for a business. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

In the case of text values, the class label should follow the schema.org <a href="https://schema.org/docs/styleguide.html">style guide</a>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPawnShop" title="http://schema.org/PawnShop"></a> Class: PawnShop <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PawnShop)</small>

A shop that will buy, or lend money against the security of, personal possessions.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPaymentCard" title="http://schema.org/PaymentCard"></a> Class: PaymentCard <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PaymentCard)</small>

A payment method using a credit, debit, store or other card to associate the payment with an account.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPaymentMethod" title="http://schema.org/PaymentMethod"></a> Class: PaymentMethod <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PaymentMethod)</small>

A payment method is a standardized procedure for transferring the monetary amount for a purchase. Payment methods are characterized by the legal and technical structures used, and by the organization or group carrying out the transaction. The following legacy values should be accepted: \n\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByBankTransferInAdvance\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByInvoice\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Cash\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#CheckInAdvance\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#COD\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DirectDebit\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#GoogleCheckout\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PayPal\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PaySwarm\n\nStructured values, or [UNCE payment means](https://vocabulary.uncefact.org/PaymentMeans) are recommended or for newer annotations.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPeriodical" title="http://schema.org/Periodical"></a> Class: Periodical <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Periodical)</small>

A publication in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended to continue indefinitely, such as a magazine, scholarly journal, or newspaper.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPhysicalActivity" title="http://schema.org/PhysicalActivity"></a> Class: PhysicalActivity <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PhysicalActivity)</small>

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPlanAction" title="http://schema.org/PlanAction"></a> Class: PlanAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PlanAction)</small>

The act of planning the execution of an event/task/action/reservation/plan to a future date.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPlay" title="http://schema.org/Play"></a> Class: Play <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Play)</small>

A play is a form of literature, usually consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance rather than just reading. Note: A performance of a Play would be a [[TheaterEvent]] or [[BroadcastEvent]] - the *Play* being the [[workPerformed]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPlayAction" title="http://schema.org/PlayAction"></a> Class: PlayAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PlayAction)</small>

The act of playing/exercising/training/performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competition or exercise.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[ListenAction]]: Unlike ListenAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to performing for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming music.\n* [[WatchAction]]: Unlike WatchAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to showing/displaying for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming visual content.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPodcastSeason" title="http://schema.org/PodcastSeason"></a> Class: PodcastSeason <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PodcastSeason)</small>

A single season of a podcast. Many podcasts do not break down into separate seasons. In that case, PodcastSeries should be used.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

A podcast is an episodic series of digital audio or video files which a user can download and listen to.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmaintainer" title="http://schema.org/maintainer">maintainer</a> | No | A maintainer of a [[Dataset]], software package ([[SoftwareApplication]]), or other [[Project]]. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FbranchOf" title="http://schema.org/branchOf">branchOf</a> | No | The larger organization that this local business is a branch of, if any. Not to be confused with (anatomical) [[branch]]. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FcurrenciesAccepted" title="http://schema.org/currenciesAccepted">currenciesAccepted</a> | No | The currency accepted.\n\nUse standard formats: [ISO 4217 currency format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217), e.g. "USD"; [Ticker symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cryptocurrencies) for cryptocurrencies, e.g. "BTC"; well known names for [Local Exchange Trading Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_exchange_trading_system) (LETS) and other currency types, e.g. "Ithaca HOUR". | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FfloorLevel" title="http://schema.org/floorLevel">floorLevel</a> | No | The floor level for an [[Accommodation]] in a multi-storey building. Since counting systems [vary internationally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storey#Consecutive_number_floor_designations), the local system should be used where possible. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FopeningHours" title="http://schema.org/openingHours">openingHours</a> | No | The general opening hours for a business. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. #### Properties from Thing

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasCredential" title="http://schema.org/hasCredential">hasCredential</a> | No | A credential awarded to the Person or Organization. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCredential" title="http://schema.org/Credential">Credential</a> |  |

This URL should conform to the particular requirements of digital links. The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. In the case of text values, the class label should follow the schema.org <a href="https://schema.org/docs/styleguide.html">style guide</a>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fdescription" title="http://schema.org/description">description</a> | No | A description of the item. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FTextObject" title="http://schema.org/TextObject">TextObject</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPriceSpecification" title="http://schema.org/PriceSpecification"></a> Class: PriceSpecification <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PriceSpecification)</small>

A structured value representing a price or price range. Typically, only the subclasses of this type are used for markup. It is recommended to use [[MonetaryAmount]] to describe independent amounts of money such as a salary, credit card limits, etc.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProduct" title="http://schema.org/Product"></a> Class: Product <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Product)</small>

Any offered product or service. For example: a pair of shoes; a concert ticket; the rental of a car; a haircut; or an episode of a TV show streamed online.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

GTINs identify trade items, including products and services, using numeric identification codes. A correct [[gtin]] value should be a valid GTIN, which means that it should be an all-numeric string of either 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits, or a "GS1 Digital Link" URL based on such a string. The numeric component should also have a [valid GS1 check digit](https://www.gs1.org/services/check-digit-calculator) and meet the other rules for valid GTINs. See also [GS1's GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) and [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Trade_Item_Number) for more details. Left-padding of the gtin values is not required or encouraged. The [[gtin]] property generalizes the earlier [[gtin8]], [[gtin12]], [[gtin13]], and [[gtin14]] properties. The GS1 [digital link specifications](https://www.gs1.org/standards/Digital-Link/) expresses GTINs as URLs (URIs, IRIs, etc.). Digital Links should be populated into the [[hasGS1DigitalLink]] attribute. Note also that this is a definition for how to include GTINs in Schema.org data, and not a definition of GTINs in general - see the GS1 documentation for authoritative details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin12" title="http://schema.org/gtin12">gtin12</a> | No | The GTIN-12 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. The GTIN-12 is the 12-digit GS1 Identification Key composed of a U.P.C. Company Prefix, Item Reference, and Check Digit used to identify trade items. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin13" title="http://schema.org/gtin13">gtin13</a> | No | The GTIN-13 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This is equivalent to 13-digit ISBN codes and EAN UCC-13. Former 12-digit UPC codes can be converted into a GTIN-13 code by simply adding a preceding zero. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fgtin8" title="http://schema.org/gtin8">gtin8</a> | No | The GTIN-8 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This code is also known as EAN/UCC-8 or 8-digit EAN. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasGS1DigitalLink" title="http://schema.org/hasGS1DigitalLink">hasGS1DigitalLink</a> | No | The <a href="https://www.gs1.org/standards/gs1-digital-link">GS1 digital link</a> associated with the object. This URL should conform to the particular requirements of digital links. The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

The general trend in web technology is towards [responsive design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsive_web_design) in which content can be flexibly adapted to a wide range of browsing environments. Pages and sites referenced with the long-established [[url]] property should ideally also be usable on a wide variety of devices, including mobile phones. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProductCollection" title="http://schema.org/ProductCollection"></a> Class: ProductCollection <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ProductCollection)</small>

A set of products (either [[ProductGroup]]s or specific variants) that are listed together e.g. in an [[Offer]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FtemporalCoverage" title="http://schema.org/temporalCoverage">temporalCoverage</a> | No | The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in [ISO 8601 time interval format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals). In the case of a Dataset it will typically indicate the relevant time period in a precise notation (e.g. for a 2011 census dataset, the year 2011 would be written "2011/2012"). Other forms of content, e.g. ScholarlyArticle, Book, TVSeries or TVEpisode, may indicate their temporalCoverage in broader terms - textually or via well-known URL. This is tentative and might be updated in future when ISO 8601 is officially updated. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDateTime" title="http://schema.org/DateTime">DateTime</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Ftext" title="http://schema.org/text">text</a> | No | The textual content of this CreativeWork. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProductGroup" title="http://schema.org/ProductGroup"></a> Class: ProductGroup <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ProductGroup)</small>

A ProductGroup represents a group of [[Product]]s that vary only in certain well-described ways, such as by [[size]], [[color]], [[material]] etc. While a ProductGroup itself is not directly offered for sale, the various varying products that it represents can be. The ProductGroup serves as a prototype or template, standing in for all of the products who have an [[isVariantOf]] relationship to it. As such, properties (including additional types) can be applied to the ProductGroup to represent characteristics shared by each of the (possibly very many) variants. Properties that reference a ProductGroup are not included in this mechanism; neither are the following specific properties [[variesBy]], [[hasVariant]], [[url]]. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProductModel" title="http://schema.org/ProductModel"></a> Class: ProductModel <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ProductModel)</small>

A datasheet or vendor specification of a product (in the sense of a prototypical description).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

In the case of [[ProductModel]], this is a pointer (from a ProductModel) to a base product from which this product is a variant. It is safe to infer that the variant inherits all product features from the base model, unless defined locally. This is not transitive. In the case of a [[ProductGroup]], the group description also serves as a template, representing a set of Products that vary on explicitly defined, specific dimensions only (so it defines both a set of variants, as well as which values distinguish amongst those variants). ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProfessionalService" title="http://schema.org/ProfessionalService"></a> Class: ProfessionalService <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ProfessionalService)</small>

Original definition: "provider of professional services."\n\nThe general [[ProfessionalService]] type for local businesses was deprecated due to confusion with [[Service]]. For reference, the types that it included were: [[Dentist]], [[AccountingService]], [[Attorney]], [[Notary]], as well as types for several kinds of [[HomeAndConstructionBusiness]]: [[Electrician]], [[GeneralContractor]], [[HousePainter]], [[Locksmith]], [[Plumber]], [[RoofingContractor]]. [[LegalService]] was introduced as a more inclusive supertype of [[Attorney]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FtemporalCoverage" title="http://schema.org/temporalCoverage">temporalCoverage</a> | No | The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in [ISO 8601 time interval format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals). This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. In the case of text values, the class label should follow the schema.org <a href="https://schema.org/docs/styleguide.html">style guide</a>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fname" title="http://schema.org/name">name</a> | No | The name of the item. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPropertyValue" title="http://schema.org/PropertyValue"></a> Class: PropertyValue <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PropertyValue)</small>

A property-value pair, e.g. representing a feature of a product or place. Use the 'name' property for the name of the property. If there is an additional human-readable version of the value, put that into the 'description' property.\n\n Always use specific schema.org properties when a) they exist and b) you can populate them. Using PropertyValue as a substitute will typically not trigger the same effect as using the original, specific property. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmeasurementMethod" title="http://schema.org/measurementMethod">measurementMethod</a> | No | A subproperty of [[measurementTechnique]] that can be used for specifying specific methods, in particular via [[MeasurementMethodEnum]]. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDefinedTerm" title="http://schema.org/DefinedTerm">DefinedTerm</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMeasurementMethodEnum" title="http://schema.org/MeasurementMethodEnum">MeasurementMethodEnum</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmeasurementTechnique" title="http://schema.org/measurementTechnique">measurementTechnique</a> | No | A technique, method or technology used in an [[Observation]], [[StatisticalVariable]] or [[Dataset]] (or [[DataDownload]], [[DataCatalog]]), corresponding to the method used for measuring the corresponding variable(s) (for datasets, described using [[variableMeasured]]; for [[Observation]], a [[StatisticalVariable]]). Often but not necessarily each [[variableMeasured]] will have an explicit representation as (or mapping to) an property such as those defined in Schema.org, or other RDF vocabularies and "knowledge graphs". In that case the subproperty of [[variableMeasured]] called [[measuredProperty]] is applicable. The [[measurementTechnique]] property helps when extra clarification is needed about how a [[measuredProperty]] was measured. This is oriented towards scientific and scholarly dataset publication but may have broader applicability; it is not intended as a full representation of measurement, but can often serve as a high level summary for dataset discovery. For example, if [[variableMeasured]] is: molecule concentration, [[measurementTechnique]] could be: "mass spectrometry" or "nmr spectroscopy" or "colorimetry" or "immunofluorescence". If the [[variableMeasured]] is "depression rating", the [[measurementTechnique]] could be "Zung Scale" or "HAM-D" or "Beck Depression Inventory". If there are several [[variableMeasured]] properties recorded for some given data object, use a [[PropertyValue]] for each [[variableMeasured]] and attach the corresponding [[measurementTechnique]]. The value can also be from an enumeration, organized as a [[MeasurementMethodEnum]]. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDefinedTerm" title="http://schema.org/DefinedTerm">DefinedTerm</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMeasurementMethodEnum" title="http://schema.org/MeasurementMethodEnum">MeasurementMethodEnum</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

Standards bodies should promote a standard prefix for the identifiers of properties from their standards. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProtein" title="http://schema.org/Protein"></a> Class: Protein <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Protein)</small>

Protein is here used in its widest possible definition, as classes of amino acid based molecules. Amyloid-beta Protein in human (UniProt P05067), eukaryota (e.g. an OrthoDB group) or even a single molecule that one can point to are all of type :Protein. A protein can thus be a subclass of another protein, e.g. :Protein as a UniProt record can have multiple isoforms inside it which would also be :Protein. They can be imagined, synthetic, hypothetical or naturally occurring.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPublicToilet" title="http://schema.org/PublicToilet"></a> Class: PublicToilet <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PublicToilet)</small>

A public toilet is a room or small building containing one or more toilets (and possibly also urinals) which is available for use by the general public, or by customers or employees of certain businesses.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPublicationEvent" title="http://schema.org/PublicationEvent"></a> Class: PublicationEvent <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PublicationEvent)</small>

A PublicationEvent corresponds indifferently to the event of publication for a CreativeWork of any type, e.g. a broadcast event, an on-demand event, a book/journal publication via a variety of delivery media.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPublicationIssue" title="http://schema.org/PublicationIssue"></a> Class: PublicationIssue <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PublicationIssue)</small>

A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or publication volume, often numbered, usually containing a grouping of works such as articles.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog-schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPublicationVolume" title="http://schema.org/PublicationVolume"></a> Class: PublicationVolume <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/PublicationVolume)</small>

A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered. It may represent a time span, such as a year.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog-schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuestion" title="http://schema.org/Question"></a> Class: Question <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Question)</small>

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FtemporalCoverage" title="http://schema.org/temporalCoverage">temporalCoverage</a> | No | The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in [ISO 8601 time interval format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals). Written works such as books may sometimes have precise temporal coverage too, e.g. a work set in 1939 - 1945 can be indicated in ISO 8601 interval format format via "1939/1945". ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuotation" title="http://schema.org/Quotation"></a> Class: Quotation <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Quotation)</small>

A quotation. Often but not necessarily from some written work, attributable to a real world author and - if associated with a fictional character - to any fictional Person. Use [[isBasedOn]] to link to source/origin. The [[recordedIn]] property can be used to reference a Quotation from an [[Event]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. In the case of text values, the class label should follow the schema.org <a href="https://schema.org/docs/styleguide.html">style guide</a>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fdescription" title="http://schema.org/description">description</a> | No | A description of the item. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FTextObject" title="http://schema.org/TextObject">TextObject</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FtemporalCoverage" title="http://schema.org/temporalCoverage">temporalCoverage</a> | No | The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in [ISO 8601 time interval format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals). This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. In the case of text values, the class label should follow the schema.org <a href="https://schema.org/docs/styleguide.html">style guide</a>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fname" title="http://schema.org/name">name</a> | No | The name of the item. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FRealEstateListing" title="http://schema.org/RealEstateListing"></a> Class: RealEstateListing <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/RealEstateListing)</small>

A [[RealEstateListing]] is a listing that describes one or more real-estate [[Offer]]s (whose [[businessFunction]] is typically to lease out, or to sell). The [[RealEstateListing]] type itself represents the overall listing, as manifested in some [[WebPage]]. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FReceiveAction" title="http://schema.org/ReceiveAction"></a> Class: ReceiveAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ReceiveAction)</small>

The act of physically/electronically taking delivery of an object that has been transferred from an origin to a destination. Reciprocal of SendAction.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[SendAction]]: The reciprocal of ReceiveAction.\n* [[TakeAction]]: Unlike TakeAction, ReceiveAction does not imply that the ownership has been transferred (e.g. I can receive a package, but it does not mean the package is now mine).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

A recipe. For dietary restrictions covered by the recipe, a few common restrictions are enumerated via [[suitableForDiet]]. The [[keywords]] property can also be used to add more detail.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FRecommendation" title="http://schema.org/Recommendation"></a> Class: Recommendation <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Recommendation)</small>

[[Recommendation]] is a type of [[Review]] that suggests or proposes something as the best option or best course of action. Recommendations may be for products or services, or other concrete things, as in the case of a ranked list or product guide. A [[Guide]] may list multiple recommendations for different categories. For example, in a [[Guide]] about which TVs to buy, the author may have several [[Recommendation]]s.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FRegisterAction" title="http://schema.org/RegisterAction"></a> Class: RegisterAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/RegisterAction)</small>

The act of registering to be a user of a service, product or web page.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, RegisterAction implies you are registering to be a user of a service, *not* a group/team of people.\n* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting to poll for updates from the object.\n* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting updates from the object.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FRentAction" title="http://schema.org/RentAction"></a> Class: RentAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/RentAction)</small>

The act of giving money in return for temporary use, but not ownership, of an object such as a vehicle or property. For example, an agent rents a property from a landlord in exchange for a periodic payment.
