### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FReportageNewsArticle" title="http://schema.org/ReportageNewsArticle"></a> Class: ReportageNewsArticle <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ReportageNewsArticle)</small>

The [[ReportageNewsArticle]] type is a subtype of [[NewsArticle]] representing news articles which are the result of journalistic news reporting conventions. In practice many news publishers produce a wide variety of article types, many of which might be considered a [[NewsArticle]] but not a [[ReportageNewsArticle]]. For example, opinion pieces, reviews, analysis, sponsored or satirical articles, or articles that combine several of these elements. The [[ReportageNewsArticle]] type is based on a stricter ideal for "news" as a work of journalism, with articles based on factual information either observed or verified by the author, or reported and verified from knowledgeable sources. This often includes perspectives from multiple viewpoints on a particular issue (distinguishing news reports from public relations or propaganda). News reports in the [[ReportageNewsArticle]] sense de-emphasize the opinion of the author, with commentary and value judgements typically expressed elsewhere. A [[ReportageNewsArticle]] which goes deeper into analysis can also be marked with an additional type of [[AnalysisNewsArticle]]. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FarticleSection" title="http://schema.org/articleSection">articleSection</a> | No | Articles may belong to one or more 'sections' in a magazine or newspaper, such as Sports, Lifestyle, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fbackstory" title="http://schema.org/backstory">backstory</a> | No | For an [[Article]], typically a [[NewsArticle]], the backstory property provides a textual summary giving a brief explanation of why and how an article was created. In a journalistic setting this could include information about reporting process, methods, interviews, data sources, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCreativeWork" title="http://schema.org/CreativeWork">CreativeWork</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpageEnd" title="http://schema.org/pageEnd">pageEnd</a> | No | The page on which the work ends; for example "138" or "xvi". | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FInteger" title="http://schema.org/Integer">Integer</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpageStart" title="http://schema.org/pageStart">pageStart</a> | No | The page on which the work starts; for example "135" or "xiii". | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FInteger" title="http://schema.org/Integer">Integer</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fpagination" title="http://schema.org/pagination">pagination</a> | No | Any description of pages that is not separated into pageStart and pageEnd; for example, "1-6, 9, 55" or "10-12, 46-49". | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fspeakable" title="http://schema.org/speakable">speakable</a> | No | Indicates sections of a Web page that are particularly 'speakable' in the sense of being highlighted as being especially appropriate for text-to-speech conversion. Other sections of a page may also be usefully spoken in particular circumstances; the 'speakable' property serves to indicate the parts most likely to be generally useful for speech. The *speakable* property can be repeated an arbitrary number of times, with three kinds of possible 'content-locator' values: 1.) *id-value* URL references - uses *id-value* of an element in the page being annotated. The simplest use of *speakable* has (potentially relative) URL values, referencing identified sections of the document concerned. 2.) CSS Selectors - addresses content in the annotated page, e.g. via class attribute. Use the [[cssSelector]] property. 3.) XPaths - addresses content via XPaths (assuming an XML view of the content). Use the [[xpath]] property. For more sophisticated markup of speakable sections beyond simple ID references, either CSS selectors or XPath expressions to pick out document section(s) as speakable. For this we define a supporting type, [[SpeakableSpecification]] which is defined to be a possible value of the *speakable* property.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSpeakableSpecification" title="http://schema.org/SpeakableSpecification">SpeakableSpecification</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FwordCount" title="http://schema.org/wordCount">wordCount</a> | No | The number of words in the text of the CreativeWork such as an Article, Book, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FInteger" title="http://schema.org/Integer">Integer</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FReservation" title="http://schema.org/Reservation"></a> Class: Reservation <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Reservation)</small>

Describes a reservation for travel, dining or an event. Some reservations require tickets. \n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, restaurant reservations, flights, or rental cars, use [[Offer]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FReservoir" title="http://schema.org/Reservoir"></a> Class: Reservoir <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Reservoir)</small>

A reservoir of water, typically an artificially created lake, like the Lake Kariba reservoir.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FResort" title="http://schema.org/Resort"></a> Class: Resort <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Resort)</small>

A resort is a place used for relaxation or recreation, attracting visitors for holidays or vacations. Resorts are places, towns or sometimes commercial establishments operated by a single company (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resort">http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resort</a>). <br /><br /> See also the <a href="/docs/hotels.html">dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations</a>. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FRole" title="http://schema.org/Role"></a> Class: Role <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Role)</small>

Represents additional information about a relationship or property. For example a Role can be used to say that a 'member' role linking some SportsTeam to a player occurred during a particular time period. Or that a Person's 'actor' role in a Movie was for some particular characterName. Such properties can be attached to a Role entity, which is then associated with the main entities using ordinary properties like 'member' or 'actor'.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/06/16/introducing-role/).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FRoom" title="http://schema.org/Room"></a> Class: Room <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Room)</small>

A room is a distinguishable space within a structure, usually separated from other spaces by interior walls (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Room">http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Room</a>). <br /><br /> See also the <a href="/docs/hotels.html">dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations</a>. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

A schedule could be processed by applications to add forthcoming events to a calendar. An [[Event]] that is associated with a [[Schedule]] using this property should not have [[startDate]] or [[endDate]] properties. These are instead defined within the associated [[Schedule]], this avoids any ambiguity for clients using the data. The property might have repeated values to specify different schedules, e.g. for different months or seasons. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSchedule" title="http://schema.org/Schedule">Schedule</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSatiricalArticle" title="http://schema.org/SatiricalArticle"></a> Class: SatiricalArticle <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/SatiricalArticle)</small>

An [[Article]] whose content is primarily [[satirical]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire) in nature, i.e. unlikely to be literally true. A satirical article is sometimes but not necessarily also a [[NewsArticle]]. [[ScholarlyArticle]]s are also sometimes satirized.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

For something that can be commercially licensed, usageInfo can provide detailed, resource-specific information about licensing options. This property can be used alongside the license property which indicates license(s) applicable to some piece of content. The usageInfo property can provide information about other licensing options, e.g. acquiring commercial usage rights for an image that is also available under non-commercial creative commons licenses. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCreativeWork" title="http://schema.org/CreativeWork">CreativeWork</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSchedule" title="http://schema.org/Schedule"></a> Class: Schedule <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Schedule)</small>

A schedule defines a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring [[Event]]. At a minimum a schedule will specify [[repeatFrequency]] which describes the interval between occurrences of the event. Additional information can be provided to specify the schedule more precisely. This includes identifying the day(s) of the week or month when the recurring event will take place, in addition to its start and end time. Schedules may also have start and end dates to indicate when they are active, e.g. to define a limited calendar of events.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmaintainer" title="http://schema.org/maintainer">maintainer</a> | No | A maintainer of a [[Dataset]], software package ([[SoftwareApplication]]), or other [[Project]]. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSellAction" title="http://schema.org/SellAction"></a> Class: SellAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/SellAction)</small>

The act of taking money from a buyer in exchange for goods or services rendered. An agent sells an object, product, or service to a buyer for a price. Reciprocal of BuyAction.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSendAction" title="http://schema.org/SendAction"></a> Class: SendAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/SendAction)</small>

The act of physically/electronically dispatching an object for transfer from an origin to a destination. Related actions:\n\n* [[ReceiveAction]]: The reciprocal of SendAction.\n* [[GiveAction]]: Unlike GiveAction, SendAction does not imply the transfer of ownership (e.g. I can send you my laptop, but I'm not necessarily giving it to you).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSequentialArt" title="http://schema.org/SequentialArt"></a> Class: SequentialArt <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/SequentialArt)</small>

An art forms that use images deployed in a specific order for the purpose of graphic storytelling (i.e., narration of graphic stories) or conveying information. Examples of SequentialArt are Franco-Belgian Bande Dessinée, Comics in the USA and 漫画 (Manga) in Japan.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FServicePeriod" title="http://schema.org/ServicePeriod"></a> Class: ServicePeriod <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ServicePeriod)</small>

ServicePeriod represents a duration with some constraints about cutoff time and business days. This is used e.g. in shipping for handling times or transit time.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FShippingConditions" title="http://schema.org/ShippingConditions"></a> Class: ShippingConditions <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ShippingConditions)</small>

ShippingConditions represent a set of constraints and information about the conditions of shipping a product. Such conditions may apply to only a subset of the products being shipped, depending on aspects of the product like weight, size, price, destination, and others. All the specified conditions must be met for this ShippingConditions to apply.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FShippingDeliveryTime" title="http://schema.org/ShippingDeliveryTime"></a> Class: ShippingDeliveryTime <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ShippingDeliveryTime)</small>

ShippingDeliveryTime provides various pieces of information about delivery times for shipping.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

#### Properties from ShippingDeliveryTime

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FbusinessDays" title="http://schema.org/businessDays">businessDays</a> | No | Days of the week when the merchant typically operates, indicated via opening hours markup. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDayOfWeek" title="http://schema.org/DayOfWeek">DayOfWeek</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOpeningHoursSpecification" title="http://schema.org/OpeningHoursSpecification">OpeningHoursSpecification</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FcutoffTime" title="http://schema.org/cutoffTime">cutoffTime</a> | No | Order cutoff time allows merchants to describe the time after which they will no longer process orders received on that day. For orders processed after cutoff time, one day gets added to the delivery time estimate. This property is expected to be most typically used via the [[ShippingRateSettings]] publication pattern. The time is indicated using the ISO-8601 Time format, e.g. "23:30:00-05:00" would represent 6:30 pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) which is 5 hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FTime" title="http://schema.org/Time">Time</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhandlingTime" title="http://schema.org/handlingTime">handlingTime</a> | No | The typical delay between the receipt of the order and the goods either leaving the warehouse or being prepared for pickup, in case the delivery method is on site pickup. In the context of [[ShippingDeliveryTime]], Typical properties: minValue, maxValue, unitCode (d for DAY). This is by common convention assumed to mean business days (if a unitCode is used, coded as "d"), i.e. only counting days when the business normally operates. In the context of [[ShippingService]], use the [[ServicePeriod]] format, that contains the same information in a structured form, with cut-off time, business days and duration. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FServicePeriod" title="http://schema.org/ServicePeriod">ServicePeriod</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FtransitTime" title="http://schema.org/transitTime">transitTime</a> | No | The typical delay the order has been sent for delivery and the goods reach the final customer. In the context of [[ShippingDeliveryTime]], use the [[QuantitativeValue]]. Typical properties: minValue, maxValue, unitCode (d for DAY). In the context of [[ShippingConditions]], use the [[ServicePeriod]]. It has a duration (as a [[QuantitativeValue]]) and also business days and a cut-off time.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FServicePeriod" title="http://schema.org/ServicePeriod">ServicePeriod</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FShippingRateSettings" title="http://schema.org/ShippingRateSettings"></a> Class: ShippingRateSettings <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/ShippingRateSettings)</small>

A ShippingRateSettings represents re-usable pieces of shipping information. It is designed for publication on an URL that may be referenced via the [[shippingSettingsLink]] property of an [[OfferShippingDetails]]. Several occurrences can be published, distinguished and matched (i.e. identified/referenced) by their different values for [[shippingLabel]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

This URL should conform to the particular requirements of digital links. The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSizeSpecification" title="http://schema.org/SizeSpecification"></a> Class: SizeSpecification <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/SizeSpecification)</small>

Size related properties of a product, typically a size code ([[name]]) and optionally a [[sizeSystem]], [[sizeGroup]], and product measurements ([[hasMeasurement]]). In addition, the intended audience can be defined through [[suggestedAge]], [[suggestedGender]], and suggested body measurements ([[suggestedMeasurement]]).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasMeasurement" title="http://schema.org/hasMeasurement">hasMeasurement</a> | No | A measurement of an item, For example, the inseam of pants, the wheel size of a bicycle, the gauge of a screw, or the carbon footprint measured for certification by an authority. Usually an exact measurement, but can also be a range of measurements for adjustable products, for example belts and ski bindings. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FsizeGroup" title="http://schema.org/sizeGroup">sizeGroup</a> | No | The size group (also known as "size type") for a product's size. Size groups are common in the fashion industry to define size segments and suggested audiences for wearable products. Multiple values can be combined, for example "men's big and tall", "petite maternity" or "regular". | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSizeGroupEnumeration" title="http://schema.org/SizeGroupEnumeration">SizeGroupEnumeration</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FsizeSystem" title="http://schema.org/sizeSystem">sizeSystem</a> | No | The size system used to identify a product's size. Typically either a standard (for example, "GS1" or "ISO-EN13402"), country code (for example "US" or "JP"), or a measuring system (for example "Metric" or "Imperial"). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSizeSystemEnumeration" title="http://schema.org/SizeSystemEnumeration">SizeSystemEnumeration</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FsuggestedAge" title="http://schema.org/suggestedAge">suggestedAge</a> | No | The age or age range for the intended audience or person, for example 3-12 months for infants, 1-5 years for toddlers. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FsuggestedGender" title="http://schema.org/suggestedGender">suggestedGender</a> | No | The suggested gender of the intended person or audience, for example "male", "female", or "unisex". | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FGenderType" title="http://schema.org/GenderType">GenderType</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FsuggestedMeasurement" title="http://schema.org/suggestedMeasurement">suggestedMeasurement</a> | No | A suggested range of body measurements for the intended audience or person, for example inseam between 32 and 34 inches or height between 170 and 190 cm. Typically found on a size chart for wearable products. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSocialMediaPosting" title="http://schema.org/SocialMediaPosting"></a> Class: SocialMediaPosting <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/SocialMediaPosting)</small>

A post to a social media platform, including blog posts, tweets, Facebook posts, etc.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

It is common for distributions of software and data to be based on "upstream" sources. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |

This code is also known as EAN/UCC-8 or 8-digit EAN. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasAdultConsideration" title="http://schema.org/hasAdultConsideration">hasAdultConsideration</a> | No | Used to tag an item to be intended or suitable for consumption or use by adults only. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FAdultOrientedEnumeration" title="http://schema.org/AdultOrientedEnumeration">AdultOrientedEnumeration</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasCertification" title="http://schema.org/hasCertification">hasCertification</a> | No | Certification information about a product, organization, service, place, or person. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FCertification" title="http://schema.org/Certification">Certification</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasEnergyConsumptionDetails" title="http://schema.org/hasEnergyConsumptionDetails">hasEnergyConsumptionDetails</a> | No | Defines the energy efficiency Category (also known as "class" or "rating") for a product according to an international energy efficiency standard. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FEnergyConsumptionDetails" title="http://schema.org/EnergyConsumptionDetails">EnergyConsumptionDetails</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasGS1DigitalLink" title="http://schema.org/hasGS1DigitalLink">hasGS1DigitalLink</a> | No | The <a href="https://www.gs1.org/standards/gs1-digital-link">GS1 digital link</a> associated with the object. This URL should conform to the particular requirements of digital links. The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

Usually an exact measurement, but can also be a range of measurements for adjustable products, for example belts and ski bindings. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FhasMerchantReturnPolicy" title="http://schema.org/hasMerchantReturnPolicy">hasMerchantReturnPolicy</a> | No | Specifies a MerchantReturnPolicy that may be applicable. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FMerchantReturnPolicy" title="http://schema.org/MerchantReturnPolicy">MerchantReturnPolicy</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fheight" title="http://schema.org/height">height</a> | No | The height of the item. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDistance" title="http://schema.org/Distance">Distance</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FQuantitativeValue" title="http://schema.org/QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FinProductGroupWithID" title="http://schema.org/inProductGroupWithID">inProductGroupWithID</a> | No | Indicates the [[productGroupID]] for a [[ProductGroup]] that this product [[isVariantOf]].  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FisConsumableFor" title="http://schema.org/isConsumableFor">isConsumableFor</a> | No | A pointer to another product (or multiple products) for which this product is a consumable. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProduct" title="http://schema.org/Product">Product</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FisFamilyFriendly" title="http://schema.org/isFamilyFriendly">isFamilyFriendly</a> | No | Indicates whether this content is family friendly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FBoolean" title="http://schema.org/Boolean">Boolean</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FisRelatedTo" title="http://schema.org/isRelatedTo">isRelatedTo</a> | No | A pointer to another, somehow related product (or multiple products). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProduct" title="http://schema.org/Product">Product</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FService" title="http://schema.org/Service">Service</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FisSimilarTo" title="http://schema.org/isSimilarTo">isSimilarTo</a> | No | A pointer to another, functionally similar product (or multiple products). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProduct" title="http://schema.org/Product">Product</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FService" title="http://schema.org/Service">Service</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FisVariantOf" title="http://schema.org/isVariantOf">isVariantOf</a> | No | Indicates the kind of product that this is a variant of. It is safe to infer that the variant inherits all product features from the base model, unless defined locally. This is not transitive. In the case of a [[ProductGroup]], the group description also serves as a template, representing a set of Products that vary on explicitly defined, specific dimensions only (so it defines both a set of variants, as well as which values distinguish amongst those variants). When used with [[ProductGroup]], this property can apply to any [[Product]] included in the group. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProductGroup" title="http://schema.org/ProductGroup">ProductGroup</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProductModel" title="http://schema.org/ProductModel">ProductModel</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmanufacturer" title="http://schema.org/manufacturer">manufacturer</a> | No | The manufacturer of the product. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FmobileUrl" title="http://schema.org/mobileUrl">mobileUrl</a> | No | The [[mobileUrl]] property is provided for specific situations in which data consumers need to determine whether one of several provided URLs is a dedicated 'mobile site'. To discourage over-use, and reflecting intial usecases, the property is expected only on [[Product]] and [[Offer]], rather than [[Thing]]. The general trend in web technology is towards [responsive design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsive_web_design) in which content can be flexibly adapted to a wide range of browsing environments. Pages and sites referenced with the long-established [[url]] property should ideally also be usable on a wide variety of devices, including mobile phones. In most cases, it would be pointless and counter productive to attempt to update all [[url]] markup to use [[mobileUrl]] for more mobile-oriented pages. The property is intended for the case when items (primarily [[Product]] and [[Offer]]) have extra URLs hosted on an additional "mobile site" alongside the main one. It should not be taken as an endorsement of this publication style.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmodel" title="http://schema.org/model">model</a> | No | The model of the product. It is recommended to additionally provide strong product identifiers via the gtin8/gtin13/gtin14 and mpn properties. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FProductModel" title="http://schema.org/ProductModel">ProductModel</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmpn" title="http://schema.org/mpn">mpn</a> | No | The Manufacturer Part Number (MPN) of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

For symmetry In the case of a [[Review]], the property describes the [[itemReviewed]] from the perspective of the review; in the case of a [[Product]], the product itself is being described. Since product descriptions tend to emphasise positive claims, it may be relatively unusual to find [[negativeNotes]] used in this way. Nevertheless for the sake of symmetry, [[negativeNotes]] can be used on [[Product]]. The property values can be expressed either as unstructured text (repeated as necessary), or if ordered, as a list (in which case the most negative is at the beginning of the list). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FItemList" title="http://schema.org/ItemList">ItemList</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FListItem" title="http://schema.org/ListItem">ListItem</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FWebContent" title="http://schema.org/WebContent">WebContent</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Foffers" title="http://schema.org/offers">offers</a> | No | An offer to provide this item&#x2014;for example, an offer to sell a product, rent the DVD of a movie, perform a service, or give away tickets to an event. Use [[businessFunction]] to indicate the kind of transaction offered, i.e. sell, lease, etc. This property can also be used to describe a [[Demand]]. While this property is listed as expected on a number of common types, it can be used in others. In that case, using a second type, such as Product or a subtype of Product, can clarify the nature of the offer.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDemand" title="http://schema.org/Demand">Demand</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOffer" title="http://schema.org/Offer">Offer</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fpattern" title="http://schema.org/pattern">pattern</a> | No | A pattern that something has, for example 'polka dot', 'striped', 'Canadian flag'. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpositiveNotes" title="http://schema.org/positiveNotes">positiveNotes</a> | No | Provides positive considerations regarding something, for example product highlights or (alongside [[negativeNotes]]) pro/con lists for reviews. In the case of a [[Review]], the property describes the [[itemReviewed]] from the perspective of the review; in the case of a [[Product]], the product itself is being described. The property values can be expressed either as unstructured text (repeated as necessary), or if ordered, as a list (in which case the most positive is at the beginning of the list). | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FItemList" title="http://schema.org/ItemList">ItemList</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FListItem" title="http://schema.org/ListItem">ListItem</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FWebContent" title="http://schema.org/WebContent">WebContent</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpurchaseDate" title="http://schema.org/purchaseDate">purchaseDate</a> | No | The date the item, e.g. vehicle, was purchased by the current owner. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDate" title="http://schema.org/Date">Date</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FreleaseDate" title="http://schema.org/releaseDate">releaseDate</a> | No | The release date of a product or product model. This can be used to distinguish the exact variant of a product. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FDate" title="http://schema.org/Date">Date</a> |  |

This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSpeakableSpecification" title="http://schema.org/SpeakableSpecification"></a> Class: SpeakableSpecification <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/SpeakableSpecification)</small>

A SpeakableSpecification indicates (typically via [[xpath]] or [[cssSelector]]) sections of a document that are highlighted as particularly [[speakable]]. Instances of this type are expected to be used primarily as values of the [[speakable]] property.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSpecialAnnouncement" title="http://schema.org/SpecialAnnouncement"></a> Class: SpecialAnnouncement <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/SpecialAnnouncement)</small>

A SpecialAnnouncement combines a simple date-stamped textual information update with contextualized Web links and other structured data. It represents an information update made by a locally-oriented organization, for example schools, pharmacies, healthcare providers, community groups, police, local government. For work in progress guidelines on Coronavirus-related markup see [this doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14ikaGCKxo50rRM7nvKSlbUpjyIk2WMQd3IkB1lItlrM/edit#). The motivating scenario for SpecialAnnouncement is the [Coronavirus pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_coronavirus_pandemic), and the initial vocabulary is oriented to this urgent situation. Schema.org expect to improve the markup iteratively as it is deployed and as feedback emerges from use. In addition to our usual [Github entry](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/2490), feedback comments can also be provided in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fpdFFxk8s87CWwACs53SGkYv3aafSxz_DTtOQxMrBJQ/edit#). While this schema is designed to communicate urgent crisis-related information, it is not the same as an emergency warning technology like [CAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Alerting_Protocol), although there may be overlaps. The intent is to cover the kinds of everyday practical information being posted to existing websites during an emergency situation. Several kinds of information can be provided: We encourage the provision of "name", "text", "datePosted", "expires" (if appropriate), "category" and "url" as a simple baseline. It is important to provide a value for "category" where possible, most ideally as a well known URL from Wikipedia or Wikidata. In the case of the 2019-2020 Coronavirus pandemic, this should be "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2019-20\_coronavirus\_pandemic" or "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q81068910". For many of the possible properties, values can either be simple links or an inline description, depending on whether a summary is available. For a link, provide just the URL of the appropriate page as the property's value. For an inline description, use a [[WebContent]] type, and provide the url as a property of that, alongside at least a simple "[[text]]" summary of the page. It is unlikely that a single SpecialAnnouncement will need all of the possible properties simultaneously. We expect that in many cases the page referenced might contain more specialized structured data, e.g. contact info, [[openingHours]], [[Event]], [[FAQPage]] etc. By linking to those pages from a [[SpecialAnnouncement]] you can help make it clearer that the events are related to the situation (e.g. Coronavirus) indicated by the [[category]] property of the [[SpecialAnnouncement]]. Many [[SpecialAnnouncement]]s will relate to particular regions and to identifiable local organizations. Use [[spatialCoverage]] for the region, and [[announcementLocation]] to indicate specific [[LocalBusiness]]es and [[CivicStructure]]s. If the announcement affects both a particular region and a specific location (for example, a library closure that serves an entire region), use both [[spatialCoverage]] and [[announcementLocation]]. The [[about]] property can be used to indicate entities that are the focus of the announcement. We now recommend using [[about]] only for representing non-location entities (e.g. a [[Course]] or a [[RadioStation]]). For places, use [[announcementLocation]] and [[spatialCoverage]]. Consumers of this markup should be aware that the initial design encouraged the use of [[about]] for locations too. The basic content of [[SpecialAnnouncement]] is similar to that of an [RSS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSS) or [Atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom_(Web_standard)) feed. For publishers without such feeds, basic feed-like information can be shared by posting [[SpecialAnnouncement]] updates in a page, e.g. using JSON-LD. For sites with Atom/RSS functionality, you can point to a feed with the [[webFeed]] property. This can be a simple URL, or an inline [[DataFeed]] object, with [[encodingFormat]] providing media type information, e.g. "application/rss+xml" or "application/atom+xml". 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). Where `XXXX` is a 4 digit _ICD_ (International Code Designator), `YYYYYY` is an _OID_ (Organization Identifier) with all formatting characters (dots, dashes, spaces) removed with a maximal length of 35 characters, and `ZZZ` is an optional OPI (Organization Part Identifier) with a maximum length of 35 characters. The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. If possible, ISO-6523 codes should be preferred to populating [vatID](https://schema.org/vatID) or [taxID](https://schema.org/taxID), as ISO identifiers are less ambiguous. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FStatement" title="http://schema.org/Statement"></a> Class: Statement <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Statement)</small>

A statement about something, for example a fun or interesting fact. If known, the main entity this statement is about can be indicated using mainEntity. For more formal claims (e.g. in Fact Checking), consider using [[Claim]] instead. Use the [[text]] property to capture the text of the statement.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmaintainer" title="http://schema.org/maintainer">maintainer</a> | No | A maintainer of a [[Dataset]], software package ([[SoftwareApplication]]), or other [[Project]]. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FStatisticalPopulation" title="http://schema.org/StatisticalPopulation"></a> Class: StatisticalPopulation <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/StatisticalPopulation)</small>

A StatisticalPopulation is a set of instances of a certain given type that satisfy some set of constraints. The property [[populationType]] is used to specify the type. Any property that can be used on instances of that type can appear on the statistical population. For example, a [[StatisticalPopulation]] representing all [[Person]]s with a [[homeLocation]] of East Podunk California would be described by applying the appropriate [[homeLocation]] and [[populationType]] properties to a [[StatisticalPopulation]] item that stands for that set of people. The properties [[numConstraints]] and [[constraintProperty]] are used to specify which of the populations properties are used to specify the population. Note that the sense of "population" used here is the general sense of a statistical population, and does not imply that the population consists of people. For example, a [[populationType]] of [[Event]] or [[NewsArticle]] could be used. See also [[Observation]], where a [[populationType]] such as [[Person]] or [[Event]] can be indicated directly. In most cases it may be better to use [[StatisticalVariable]] instead of [[StatisticalPopulation]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FStatisticalVariable" title="http://schema.org/StatisticalVariable"></a> Class: StatisticalVariable <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/StatisticalVariable)</small>

[[StatisticalVariable]] represents any type of statistical metric that can be measured at a place and time. The usage pattern for [[StatisticalVariable]] is typically expressed using [[Observation]] with an explicit [[populationType]], which is a type, typically drawn from Schema.org. Each [[StatisticalVariable]] is marked as a [[ConstraintNode]], meaning that some properties (those listed using [[constraintProperty]]) serve in this setting solely to define the statistical variable rather than literally describe a specific person, place or thing. For example, a [[StatisticalVariable]] Median_Height_Person_Female representing the median height of women, could be written as follows: the population type is [[Person]]; the measuredProperty [[height]]; the [[statType]] [[median]]; the [[gender]] [[Female]]. It is important to note that there are many kinds of scientific quantitative observation which are not fully, perfectly or unambiguously described following this pattern, or with solely Schema.org terminology. The approach taken here is designed to allow partial, incremental or minimal description of [[StatisticalVariable]]s, and the use of detailed sets of entity and property IDs from external repositories. The [[measurementMethod]], [[unitCode]] and [[unitText]] properties can also be used to clarify the specific nature and notation of an observed measurement. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fiso6523Code" title="http://schema.org/iso6523Code">iso6523Code</a> | No | An organization identifier as defined in [ISO 6523(-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523). The various components (ICD, OID, OPI) are joined with a colon character (ASCII `0x3a`). Note that many existing organization identifiers defined as attributes like [leiCode](https://schema.org/leiCode) (`0199`), [duns](https://schema.org/duns) (`0060`) or [GLN](https://schema.org/globalLocationNumber) (`0088`) can be expressed using ISO-6523. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSubscribeAction" title="http://schema.org/SubscribeAction"></a> Class: SubscribeAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/SubscribeAction)</small>

The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates pushed to.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, SubscribeAction implies that the subscriber acts as a passive agent being constantly/actively pushed for updates.\n* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.\n* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSuite" title="http://schema.org/Suite"></a> Class: Suite <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Suite)</small>

A suite in a hotel or other public accommodation, denotes a class of luxury accommodations, the key feature of which is multiple rooms (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suite_(hotel)">http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suite_(hotel)</a>). <br /><br /> See also the <a href="/docs/hotels.html">dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations</a>. 

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FSuperficialAnatomy" title="http://schema.org/SuperficialAnatomy"></a> Class: SuperficialAnatomy <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/SuperficialAnatomy)</small>

Anatomical features that can be observed by sight (without dissection), including the form and proportions of the human body as well as surface landmarks that correspond to deeper subcutaneous structures. Superficial anatomy plays an important role in sports medicine, phlebotomy, and other medical specialties as underlying anatomical structures can be identified through surface palpation. For example, during back surgery, superficial anatomy can be used to palpate and count vertebrae to find the site of incision. Or in phlebotomy, superficial anatomy can be used to locate an underlying vein; for example, the median cubital vein can be located by palpating the borders of the cubital fossa (such as the epicondyles of the humerus) and then looking for the superficial signs of the vein, such as size, prominence, ability to refill after depression, and feel of surrounding tissue support. As another example, in a subluxation (dislocation) of the glenohumeral joint, the bony structure becomes pronounced with the deltoid muscle failing to cover the glenohumeral joint allowing the edges of the scapula to be superficially visible. Here, the superficial anatomy is the visible edges of the scapula, implying the underlying dislocation of the joint (the related anatomical structure).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FopeningHours" title="http://schema.org/openingHours">openingHours</a> | No | The general opening hours for a business. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

For example, the motion picture known as "Ghostbusters" has a titleEIDR of "10.5240/7EC7-228A-510A-053E-CBB8-J". This title (or work) may have several variants, which EIDR calls "edits". See [[editEIDR]]. Since schema.org types like [[Movie]], [[TVEpisode]], [[TVSeason]], and [[TVSeries]] can be used for both works and their multiple expressions, it is possible to use [[titleEIDR]] alone (for a general description), or alongside [[editEIDR]] for a more edit-specific description.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2Fmaintainer" title="http://schema.org/maintainer">maintainer</a> | No | A maintainer of a [[Dataset]], software package ([[SoftwareApplication]]), or other [[Project]]. When [[maintainer]] is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a [[Dataset]], it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The [[isBasedOn]] property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.  | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FOrganization" title="http://schema.org/Organization">Organization</a>, <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPerson" title="http://schema.org/Person">Person</a> |  |

In the latter case, multiple matches within a page can constitute a single conceptual "Web page element". | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FXPathType" title="http://schema.org/XPathType">XPathType</a> |  |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FfloorLevel" title="http://schema.org/floorLevel">floorLevel</a> | No | The floor level for an [[Accommodation]] in a multi-storey building. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

The *speakable* property can be repeated an arbitrary number of times, with three kinds of possible 'content-locator' values: 1.) *id-value* URL references - uses *id-value* of an element in the page being annotated. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FTherapeuticProcedure" title="http://schema.org/TherapeuticProcedure"></a> Class: TherapeuticProcedure <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/TherapeuticProcedure)</small>

A medical procedure intended primarily for therapeutic purposes, aimed at improving a health condition.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FTouristAttraction" title="http://schema.org/TouristAttraction"></a> Class: TouristAttraction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/TouristAttraction)</small>

A tourist attraction. In principle any Thing can be a [[TouristAttraction]], from a [[Mountain]] and [[LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings]] to a [[LocalBusiness]]. This Type can be used on its own to describe a general [[TouristAttraction]], or be used as an [[additionalType]] to add tourist attraction properties to any other type. (See examples below)

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FTouristDestination" title="http://schema.org/TouristDestination"></a> Class: TouristDestination <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/TouristDestination)</small>

A tourist destination. In principle any [[Place]] can be a [[TouristDestination]] from a [[City]], Region or [[Country]] to an [[AmusementPark]] or [[Hotel]]. This Type can be used on its own to describe a general [[TouristDestination]], or be used as an [[additionalType]] to add tourist relevant properties to any other [[Place]]. A [[TouristDestination]] is defined as a [[Place]] that contains, or is colocated with, one or more [[TouristAttraction]]s, often linked by a similar theme or interest to a particular [[touristType]]. The [UNWTO](http://www2.unwto.org/) defines Destination (main destination of a tourism trip) as the place visited that is central to the decision to take the trip. (See examples below.)

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FTouristTrip" title="http://schema.org/TouristTrip"></a> Class: TouristTrip <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/TouristTrip)</small>

A tourist trip. A created itinerary of visits to one or more places of interest ([[TouristAttraction]]/[[TouristDestination]]) often linked by a similar theme, geographic area, or interest to a particular [[touristType]]. The [UNWTO](http://www2.unwto.org/) defines tourism trip as the Trip taken by visitors. (See examples below.)

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. For example, 3pm is specified as ```15:00```, 10am as ```10:00```. \n* Here is an example: <code>&lt;time itemprop="openingHours" datetime=&quot;Tu,Th 16:00-20:00&quot;&gt;Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm&lt;/time&gt;</code>.\n* If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <code>&lt;time itemprop=&quot;openingHours&quot; datetime=&quot;Mo-Su&quot;&gt;Monday through Sunday, all day&lt;/time&gt;</code>. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpaymentAccepted" title="http://schema.org/paymentAccepted">paymentAccepted</a> | No | Cash, Credit Card, Cryptocurrency, Local Exchange Tradings System, etc. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |
| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FpriceRange" title="http://schema.org/priceRange">priceRange</a> | No | The price range of the business, for example ```$$$```. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FText" title="http://schema.org/Text">Text</a> |  |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FTrackAction" title="http://schema.org/TrackAction"></a> Class: TrackAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/TrackAction)</small>

An agent tracks an object for updates.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, TrackAction refers to the interest on the location of innanimates objects.\n* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, TrackAction refers to the interest on the location of innanimate objects.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FTradeAction" title="http://schema.org/TradeAction"></a> Class: TradeAction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/TradeAction)</small>

The act of participating in an exchange of goods and services for monetary compensation. An agent trades an object, product or service with a participant in exchange for a one time or periodic payment.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FTrainReservation" title="http://schema.org/TrainReservation"></a> Class: TrainReservation <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/TrainReservation)</small>

A reservation for train travel.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.\n\n* Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: ```Mo```, ```Tu```, ```We```, ```Th```, ```Fr```, ```Sa```, ```Su```.\n* Times are specified using 24:00 format. This URL should conform to the particular requirements of digital links. The link should only contain the Application Identifiers (AIs) that are relevant for the entity being annotated, for instance a [[Product]] or an [[Organization]], and for the correct granularity. In particular, for products:<ul><li>A Digital Link that contains a serial number (AI <code>21</code>) should only be present on instances of [[IndividualProduct]]</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a lot number (AI <code>10</code>) should be annotated as [[SomeProducts]] if only products from that lot are sold, or [[IndividualProduct]] if there is only a specific product.</li><li>A Digital Link that contains a global model number (AI <code>8013</code>) should be attached to a [[Product]] or a [[ProductModel]].</li></ul> Other item types should be adapted similarly. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FURL" title="http://schema.org/URL">URL</a> |  |

UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FUserComments" title="http://schema.org/UserComments"></a> Class: UserComments <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/UserComments)</small>

UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FUserInteraction" title="http://schema.org/UserInteraction"></a> Class: UserInteraction <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/UserInteraction)</small>

UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| N/A | N/A |

UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FUserPlusOnes" title="http://schema.org/UserPlusOnes"></a> Class: UserPlusOnes <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/UserPlusOnes)</small>

UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FUserReview" title="http://schema.org/UserReview"></a> Class: UserReview <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/UserReview)</small>

A review created by an end-user (e.g. consumer, purchaser, attendee etc.), in contrast with [[CriticReview]].

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FadditionalType" title="http://schema.org/additionalType">additionalType</a> | No | An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. ### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FVacationRental" title="http://schema.org/VacationRental"></a> Class: VacationRental <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/VacationRental)</small>

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

### <a id="http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FVehicle" title="http://schema.org/Vehicle"></a> Class: Vehicle <small style="color:#aaa">(http://schema.org/Vehicle)</small>

A vehicle is a device that is designed or used to transport people or cargo over land, water, air, or through space.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FdisplayLocation" title="http://schema.org/displayLocation">displayLocation</a> | No | The location at which an item can be viewed or experienced in-person. | <a href="#http%3A%2F%2Fschema.org%2FPlace" title="http://schema.org/Place">Place</a> |  |
